  - **Decision:** NA-0534 consumes D438/D437/D436/D435/D414/D413 inheritance and classifies the diagnostic as `REMOTE_FORWARD_PORT_39176_DIAGNOSTIC_MARKER_TRAVERSAL_PASS`. Remote pre-probe port-state showed no listener, the transient loopback bind probe printed `NA0534_REMOTE_LOOPBACK_BIND_PROBE_OK`, the corrected reverse-forward made `127.0.0.1:39176` visible remotely during the probe, the stdin-script trigger received `NA0534_TRIGGER_ACK_RECEIVED_OK`, and cleanup verified no local proof-root process and no remaining local or remote listener.
  - **Evidence consumed:** D438 recorded NA-0533 DONE, NA-0534 READY, classification `REMOTE_FORWARD_PORT_39176_REGRESSION_DIAGNOSTIC_IMPLEMENTATION_READY`, D-1056 and D-1057 each once, and final public-safety/advisories green. D437 recorded NA-0532 closeout restored NA-0533 after the D436 forwarding-precheck failure. D436 recorded local listener readiness, local trigger rehearsal pass, reverse-forward failure before remote trigger with `remote port forwarding failed for listen port 39176`, no marker traversal, no ACK, no qsc E2EE, no qsc send/receive, and cleanup pass. D435 recorded stdin-script trigger success with marker traversal and ACK. D414 recorded dedicated-key forwarding marker/ACK success. D413 recorded the accepted dedicated forwarding key proof with fingerprint `SHA256:7guT/Hd72vuu+u1Jrwpuy0hSFETVrxYaXHwupuFfaPM`, public key comment `qsl-inspiron-qslcodex-forward-20260622`, and loopback-only `permitlisten` / `permitopen` on `127.0.0.1:39176`.
  - **Diagnostic result:** The operational `ssh -G inspiron` parse still reported `clearallforwardings yes`, so reverse forwarding used a proof-root SSH config with the dedicated key, publickey-only authentication, no agent/X11 forwarding, no PTY, no ControlMaster, and `ClearAllForwardings no`. The proof-root config contained no `ClearAllForwardings yes`. `ExitOnForwardFailure=yes` did not abort the corrected single-lifetime reverse-forward; the remote port was visible during the forward, marker traversal passed, and ACK returned. No SSH debug log redaction was required because the corrected reverse-forward did not fail.
  - **Recovered failures:** Main check-run summary and verifier commands had local Python quoting mistakes; both were corrected and recorded. The initially guessed NA-0520 testplan path was corrected by tracked-file discovery. A zero-match `grep` for `ClearAllForwardings yes` was converted to an explicit count proof with result 0. A remote boundary command initially had nested shell quoting that prevented output capture; it was rerun with direct shell quoting and passed. The first integrated marker attempt failed because local listener and forward background processes did not survive across separate command invocations; it was rerun in one shell lifetime with trap-based cleanup and passed. These recoveries did not require any scope expansion, remote file write, qsc E2EE, qsc send/receive, qsl-server, or qsl-attachments.

Classification is `LOCAL_OPS_SSD_HYGIENE_SHARED_TARGET_IMPLEMENTATION_READY`. The selected successor is `NA-0543 -- QSL Local Ops SSD Hygiene / Shared Cargo Target Implementation Harness`.

D453/D452 inheritance and the June 25 public Progress entry were reviewed. Operator cleanup context was consumed: root usage fell from 95% to about 37%, old per-lane Rust targets were removed, 1,133 old proof roots were archived to `/backup/qsl`, path-preserving symlinks were retained, and the nightly maintenance script/timer was installed as operator-owned local state.
  - **Installed maintenance inventory:** `/usr/local/sbin/qbuild-ssd-maintenance` is root:root mode 755, SHA-256 `53e9820f0ece`, default dry-run, service apply-mode ExecStart with 7-day target/proof-root ages and warn-percent 90, `/backup/qsl` mount guard, flock, active-process guard, proof-root archive to `/backup/qsl/qbuild-tmp-archive/YYYY/MM`, logs on `/backup/qsl`, and `/srv/qbuild/cache` exclusion. Service runs as root by default, has empty `SuccessExitStatus`, infinite timeout, and mount condition only. Timer is enabled/active, non-persistent, scheduled 03:30 America/Chicago with 20 minute randomized delay.
  - **Scheduled run classification:** `MAINTENANCE_NO_SCHEDULED_RUN_YET`. The timer has no last trigger and the service journal has no entries. The latest housekeeping log is an operator/manual apply run that archived 1,133 proof roots, deleted zero targets, and ended with `QBUILD_SSD_MAINTENANCE_OK`; it is not represented as a scheduled timer success.
  - **Storage/cache inventory:** `/srv/qbuild/work` is about 52G with 292 lane work directories. There are 28 remaining per-lane `qsl-protocol/target` directories totaling about 43GB. `/srv/qbuild/tmp` is about 65G with 150 live directories, 1,133 archived symlinks, and zero broken symlinks. `/srv/qbuild/cache` is about 21G; `/srv/qbuild/cache/targets/qsl-protocol` is about 17G. `/backup/qsl/qbuild-tmp-archive` is about 37G. Current disk usage is `/` 37% and `/backup/qsl` 33%.
  - **Current maintenance safety review:** The installed script is fail-closed enough for observed operator use but needs implementation hardening. Candidate age must use newest descendant mtime, not only top-level directory mtime. Active-process detection must avoid self-match and path-regex ambiguity and should consider lane/worktree recency plus dirty worktrees. Archive transactions must verify copy completeness before source removal and document `.moved.<timestamp>` recovery. systemd should treat intentional active-build skip distinctly from failure while keeping disk warnings non-success. Logs need machine-readable summaries, bounded retention, symlink verification, skipped paths, failed paths, and latest-result markers.
  - **qwork/qbuild architecture:** `qwork` resolves to `/home/victor/.local/bin/qwork`, a wrapper for `/srv/qbuild/tools/qwork.sh`; `qstart`, `qresume`, and `qbuild` were not resolvable in this shell. qwork/qbuild source is operator-owned local state, not tracked by this repository. `/srv/qbuild/tools/env_qbuild.sh` already defines `/srv/qbuild/cache/targets/<repo>` through `qbuild_target_dir`, but current qwork cannot export `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` into the parent shell that later launches Codex and does not create target symlinks or lane-local Cargo config.
  - **Shared Cargo target design:** Select option 1, qwork/qbuild-managed shared SSD target. Selected base is `/srv/qbuild/cache/targets/qsl-protocol`. Selected ordinary current partition is `/srv/qbuild/cache/targets/qsl-protocol/rustc-1.95.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/default`, tied to the observed cargo/rustc 1.95.0 host class. If NA-0543 observes a different toolchain class before implementation, it must STOP and request refreshed path authorization.
  - **Rejected options:** Lane target symlink is rejected because it confuses provenance and cleanup. Per-lane targets plus cleanup is rejected because it preserves large duplication. Global shell-profile `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is rejected because it affects unrelated repositories. Shared target on platter is rejected because ordinary builds should remain on SSD. sccache-only is rejected because sccache is not installed and would not remove duplicated target artifacts by itself.
  - **Isolated-target exceptions:** Proof-root-isolated targets remain mandatory for binary provenance/hash evidence, remote binary staging/restaging, reproducibility-sensitive builds, sanitizer/Miri/fuzz/toolchain-specialized runs when collision risk exists, directives explicitly requiring isolated build artifacts, and any case where source-to-binary attribution would otherwise be ambiguous.
  - **Environment precedence:** A directive-provided `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` wins. A preexisting operator-provided `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` wins. The ordinary qwork/qbuild shared default applies only when `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is unset. qwork must not overwrite explicit target overrides.
  - **Ownership/mode policy:** Parent `/srv/qbuild/cache/targets` may remain root:victor setgid as observed. Repo/class target directories should be victor:victor mode 2775. No global shell profile or committed Cargo config is authorized solely for local qbuild.
  - **Concurrency/locking policy:** One-lane-at-a-time governance and qwork lane locking remain primary. Future shared-target setup should use a repo/class advisory lock for setup/cleanup. Maintenance must skip when cargo/rustc/sccache/qwork/qstart/qresume activity is detected. Shared-target pressure cleanup requires active-process absence, exact path checks, and size reporting.
  - **Pressure thresholds:** Healthy below 80% root usage; warning at or above 80%; pressure at or above 85%; urgent at or above 90%; hard build/directive stop at or above 95%. Warning is report-only. Pressure and urgent cleanup require separately authorized bounded policy.
  - **Cleanup/retention/logging policy:** Normal nightly policy remains 7-day old per-lane target cleanup and 7-day old proof-root archive, `/backup/qsl` mounted, active build/qwork detection required, path-preserving archive links required, shared target excluded from routine age cleanup, and 90-day maintenance-log retention on `/backup/qsl`.
  - **Archive transaction policy:** Future implementation must preserve copy-before-cutover, verify destination mount, detect collisions, copy to archive, verify file count and byte count or rsync dry-diff before source removal, move source to `.moved.<timestamp>`, create and verify original-path symlink, and remove `.moved.<timestamp>` only after verification succeeds.
  - **Operator/Codex boundary:** Codex may mutate tracked files only. Operator-owned local actions include `/srv/qbuild/tools/env_qbuild.sh`, `/srv/qbuild/tools/qwork.sh`, `/home/victor/.local/bin/qwork`, `/usr/local/sbin/qbuild-ssd-maintenance`, `/etc/systemd/system/qbuild-ssd-maintenance.service`, `/etc/systemd/system/qbuild-ssd-maintenance.timer`, `/srv/qbuild/cache/targets/qsl-protocol/rustc-1.95.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/default`, `/backup/qsl/qbuild-tmp-archive/housekeeping-logs`, and `/backup/qsl/qbuild-local-ops-rollback/NA-0543/pre-change`. Codex must not silently perform operator-owned root/local actions.

- **ID:** D-1175
  - **Title:** NA-0592 qsc true triple-ratchet seed fallback hardening authorization
  - **Date:** 2026-07-02
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** NA-0592 consumes D-1173 and D-1174, verifies fresh qwork proof from `2026-07-02T15:58:53Z`, verifies current qsl-protocol main `HEAD`/`origin/main` at `5d79fc682098`, classifies current main public-safety, advisories, suite2-vectors, cargo audits, locked metadata, and drift health as pass with required-check visibility recovery, maps the qsc seed fallback source inventory and call graph, and classifies the fallback as `SEED_FALLBACK_RUNTIME_PRODUCTION_PATH_RISK`. The fallback is compiled into the normal qsc binary; ordinary qsc send, receive, TUI relay, and qsc file/attachment descriptor command paths can reach it when explicit environment variables are present; it requires explicit env, not an explicit CLI flag; it is not visible in top-level help; it is documented in qsc remote relay testing docs; it bypasses authenticated handshake-bound session state by synthesizing deterministic Suite2 state; it weakens runtime security if enabled; demo scripts publish seed summaries; and it is not safe to leave without hardening. The selected hardening strategy is a B/E hybrid: gate the fallback behind an explicit unsafe test-only cfg seam, move or rename retained deterministic fallback behavior as test-only helper surface, make default qsc builds ignore or reject env-only fallback, update tests/demos/docs accordingly, and preserve the verified no-seed Suite2/triple-ratchet send/receive path. Crypto/protocol/wire/auth/key-schedule/identity/transcript/state semantic redesign is not needed for this selected successor. Result classification is `SEED_FALLBACK_HARDENING_IMPLEMENTATION_READY`.

It must implement the exact D-1175-selected hardening, preserve the verified no-seed Suite2/triple-ratchet send/receive path, add fail-closed tests proving ordinary qsc send, receive, relay, and future attachment command surfaces cannot accidentally use the fallback, and keep full qsl-attachments send/receive integration deferred.

  - **Title:** NA-0604 closeout and NA-0605 restoration after qsc TLS policy proof
  - **Date:** 2026-07-05
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** NA-0604 closeout consumes D-1199 and qsl-protocol PR #1482, which merged at `2ed1d17d61d3` from implementation branch `na-0604-laptop-qsc-readiness-follow-up` with implementation commit `bcadf0dae6fc`. D-1199 exists once and is Accepted. D-1199 accepted result `NA0604_QSC_TLS_REQUIRED_POLICY_CONFIRMED`. PR #1482 post-merge public-safety and advisories completed success; suite2-vectors and qsc-adversarial-smoke were success or conclusively satisfied; CodeQL and goal-lint visibility were classified through D498-style recovery; and no failed required checks remained. NA-0604 is marked DONE, and NA-0605 is restored as exactly one READY successor.
  - **Protocol and transport clarification:** QSL/qsc is the cryptographic/content protocol. HTTP, HTTPS, SSH local-forward, Tailnet, and public internet paths are transport/carriage layers for opaque qsc/QSL envelopes and relay/control APIs. The project security objective is not HTTP/HTTPS security as the primary protocol; qsc/QSL owns encryption/decryption, protects plaintext and keys from relay/storage infrastructure, qsl-server relays opaque encrypted/control data only, and qsl-attachments stores opaque ciphertext/object data only when used. Transport protection remains required for non-loopback paths because route tokens, bearer headers, capability handles, timing, endpoint, and traffic metadata can leak at the transport layer.
  - **TLS-required policy classification:** The current direct LAN HTTP non-loopback relay endpoint shape is blocked by qsc TLS-required policy. That block is security-preserving. qsc allowing HTTP loopback is acceptable for local loopback tests. qsc accepting HTTPS non-loopback is the intended direct network transport shape. qsc rejecting HTTP non-loopback is not weakened or bypassed by this closeout.
  - **Selected successor:** NA-0605 is restored as `NA-0605 -- QSL LAN Minimal qsc E2EE Relay Verification via Operator SSH Local-Forward Harness`. SSH local-forward is selected as the safest next baby-step LAN transport shape because qsc on the laptop sees an HTTP loopback relay endpoint while SSH protects LAN carriage to the build server. SSH local-forward is not the final direct HTTPS LAN deployment proof.
  - **Boundary proof:** No NA-0605 implementation occurred. No qsc source/test/fuzz mutation occurred. No qsl-server mutation occurred. No qsl-attachments mutation or runtime action occurred. No LAN runtime test occurred in closeout. No Codex SSH to laptop occurred. No laptop SSH server setup occurred. No second Codex on laptop occurred. No Tailnet/Tailscale action occurred. - **ID:** D-1209
  - **Title:** NA-0608 LAN qsl-attachments hostile-analyst, fail-closed negatives, leakage, seed-fallback, and metadata analysis
  - **Date:** 2026-07-06
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** NA-0608 stressed and analyzed the working LAN qsl-attachments path under a hostile-analyst model, executed under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-06-541 (D541) and its Addendum A (bounded LAN runtime provisioning). D-1207 and D-1208 were each consumed once and Accepted; D-1209 was absent before this implementation. The build server provisioned a disposable runtime outside the tracked repository (qsl-server `19b9b02dbe1f` and qsl-attachments `a3ebad2fd19a` cloned at main, validated, and built; qsc built from the tracked workspace with no tracked source, dependency, or lockfile mutation) and ran qsl-server and qsl-attachments bound to 127.0.0.1 loopback only. A real two-party qsc attachment send/receive/decrypt/validate was verified with real ML-KEM/ML-DSA identities and no seed fallback (QSP v5.0, real ratchet, receiver plaintext digest matched the sender fixture).
  - **Scope direction:** Per operator direction, the hostile-analyst negatives and the leakage, seed-fallback, and metadata analyses ran on the build-host loopback harness, which exercises the same qsc-to-service fail-closed behavior as the SSH loopback-forward transport established by NA-0607 (D-1205/D-1206). NA-0608 does not re-run over the laptop forward and introduces no LAN-transport claim beyond NA-0607.
  - **Negatives result:** Every hostile-analyst negative fail-closed with a deterministic reject class and produced zero plaintext: wrong capability `REJECT_QATTSVC_FETCH_CAPABILITY`; wrong resume token `REJECT_QATTSVC_RESUME_TOKEN`/`REJECT_QATTSVC_SESSION_STATE`; corrupted object `REJECT_ATT_CIPHERTEXT_PRECHECK`; missing/deleted object `REJECT_QATTSVC_LOCATOR_UNKNOWN`; replay-like duplicate rejected at QSP header authentication; wrong route no-delivery; wrong peer no-session `protocol_inactive`. Corrupted descriptor is covered by envelope authentication (descriptor is inside the opaque QSP envelope) and was not separately exercised. No-mutation-on-reject: rejected uploads left only staged/orphan artifacts discarded by the service storage reconciliation; no committed/fetchable object or plaintext was produced.
  - **Leakage and seed fallback:** A unique-canary plaintext-marker attachment produced zero canary occurrences in attachment object storage and zero in qsl-server/qsl-attachments logs, confirming opaque ciphertext-only storage; logs emitted no plaintext, passphrase, private-key, or fetch-capability values. Seed fallback classified not_used (`QSC_ALLOW_SEED_FALLBACK`/`QSC_UNSAFE_TEST_SEED_FALLBACK` never set; no activation marker).
  - **Metadata matrix:** Plaintext body, key material, and fetch capability PROTECTED; attachment ciphertext-object size, object/part count, and upload/fetch timing EXPOSED residual metadata; route/mailbox tokens pseudonymous to the relay; sender/receiver identities PROTECTED. Classified `LAN_ATTACHMENT_METADATA_CLASSIFIED_ACCEPTABLE_FOR_NEXT_STEP`; size/count/timing residual metadata is the documented NA-0609 hardening surface.
  - **Result and successor:** Selected result `LAN_QSL_ATTACHMENTS_HOSTILE_ANALYST_FAIL_CLOSED_PASS` (loopback-harness variant). Selected successor `NA-0609 -- QSL Hostile Analyst / Metadata Minimization and Implementation-Attack Hardening Plan`, to be restored at NA-0608 closeout (D-1210). NA-0609 must not be implemented in this lane.
  - **Boundary proof:** Implementation mutates only `docs/governance/evidence/NA-0608_lan_qsl_attachments_hostile_analyst_metadata_fail_closed_harness.md`, `tests/NA-0608_lan_qsl_attachments_hostile_analyst_metadata_fail_closed_testplan.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `TRACEABILITY.md`, and `docs/ops/ROLLING_OPERATIONS_JOURNAL.md`. No qsc/qsl-server/qsl-attachments tracked source, test, dependency, lockfile, or workflow mutation occurred; the disposable runtime clones and builds were outside the tracked repository and were not committed. No protocol behavior change occurred. No qwork/qstart/qresume execution, sudo, systemd, firewall, package install, Tailnet/Tailscale, workflow dispatch/rerun, branch-protection or repo-settings mutation occurred. The qscwork remote action was limited to the authorized account and its owned test workspace with no personal file access.

- **ID:** D-1213
  - **Title:** NA-0609B qsc handshake and identity read-only security audit (LITE-CEREMONY)
  - **Date:** 2026-07-06
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** NA-0609B is an inserted read-only security audit lane executed under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-06-543 (D543), the first LITE-CEREMONY lane (single PR, single decision). It does not implement NA-0609 and applies no fix. D-1211 and D-1212 were each consumed once and Accepted; D-1213 was absent before this implementation. Applying the NA-0609A Director triage discipline, the lane audited the highest-yield security seam (DOC-AUD-001 §4.1: qsc handshake execution + identity) and resolved ledger ENG-0001.
  - **LITE-CEREMONY certification:** The lane reads security-critical code but mutates only docs/evidence/ledger/governance paths; it changes no `.rs`, test, Cargo, workflow, canonical spec, `.claude`, or hook file, adds no test, takes no runtime/LAN action, and defers every fix to a separate full-ritual remediation lane. It therefore qualifies as a read-only-audit LITE-CEREMONY lane per DOC-OPS-006 §9.
  - **Result:** `QSC_HANDSHAKE_IDENTITY_AUDIT_COMPLETE_NO_P0_P1_THREE_P3_HARDENING`. No P0 or P1 was substantiated; no stop-and-escalate was triggered. The handshake seam was verified sound on: transcript binding over `A1||B1` keyed by the hybrid PQ-init secret with domain separation and suite-context binding; ML-KEM + X25519 hybrid with an all-zero DH-pubkey guard; fail-closed ML-DSA-65 signature verification; suite-context downgrade binding and rejection (G3); a coherent dual-pin identity model (primary KEM identity fingerprint == the `identity show` value, plus an optional ML-DSA fingerprint pin) with fail-closed peer_mismatch; no-mutation-on-reject across all three accept sub-paths (session store only after MAC + signature + identity verification); accurate operator markers; atomic temp+fsync+rename config/session writes; and session_id-bound replay rejection.
  - **Findings (ranked, DOC-AUD-001 §6; routed to the ledger):** ENG-0003 (P3) non-constant-time keyed-MAC comparisons at handshake/mod.rs:1458 and :1665 with no constant-time helper in the stack (low exploitability due to the ML-DSA signature second factor and fresh per-session keys; systematic; recommended for the NA-0609 implementation-attack hardening batch). ENG-0004 (P3) `fsync_dir_best_effort` is a no-op at fs_store/mod.rs:359 so atomic-rename directory durability is not guaranteed on power-loss (fail-closed-safe direction; a G2 gap). ENG-0001 (P3, resolved-into-finding) the fingerprint model is coherent; the residual is a silent `--as <label>` self-identity divergence footgun. ENG-0002 remains out of handshake scope on the attachment track.
  - **Boundary proof:** Implementation mutates only `docs/governance/evidence/NA-0609B_qsc_handshake_identity_security_audit_harness.md`, `tests/NA-0609B_qsc_handshake_identity_security_audit_testplan.md`, `docs/ops/IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md`, `NEXT_ACTIONS.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `TRACEABILITY.md`, and `docs/ops/ROLLING_OPERATIONS_JOURNAL.md`. No public-readiness, production-readiness, security-completion, crypto-complete, external-review-complete, formal-proof-complete, vulnerability-free, or bug-free claim is made; this is a bounded internal read-only audit.

- **ID:** D-1214
  - **Title:** NA-0609C constant-time handshake MAC comparison hardening (ENG-0003 remediation)
  - **Date:** 2026-07-06
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** NA-0609C is the bounded remediation lane for ledger ENG-0003 (from the NA-0609B audit), executed under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-06-544 (D544). D-1212 and D-1213 were each consumed once and Accepted; D-1214 was absent before this implementation. The lane makes the two handshake keyed-MAC comparisons constant-time and closes ENG-0003. This is a timing-only security-hardening change: the comparison result, accept/reject semantics, markers, and wire format are bit-for-bit unchanged; only the comparison no longer short-circuits on the first differing byte.
  - **Change:** In `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/handshake/mod.rs`, added a dependency-free helper `hs_ct_eq_32(a: &[u8; 32], b: &[u8; 32]) -> bool` (XOR-accumulate, no early-out) and replaced `if mac != resp.mac` (B1 transcript MAC) with `if !hs_ct_eq_32(&mac, &resp.mac)` and `if expect != confirm.mac` (A2 confirm MAC) with `if !hs_ct_eq_32(&expect, &confirm.mac)`. Added a co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod ct_eq_tests` proving `hs_ct_eq_32` is equal to `==` for equal inputs, single-byte flips at every position, a high-bit flip, an all-different case, and mixed vectors. No new dependency was added (`subtle` was intentionally avoided to keep the change dependency-free and in scope). No other source file, no Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, and no MAC/transcript/signature/derivation/wire-format was changed.
  - **Semantic-equivalence proof:** For any `a, b: [u8; 32]`, `hs_ct_eq_32(a, b)` is `true` iff every XOR byte is zero iff `a == b`; therefore `!hs_ct_eq_32(&x, &y)` equals `x != y` bit-for-bit. Validated by the new unit tests (4 pass) and by the existing handshake suites passing unchanged: `handshake_mvp` (10), `handshake_contract_na0217i` (1), `handshake_security_closure` (4), `kem_signature_transcript_binding_negative` (5), `handshake_provider_error_no_mutation` (1). `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build`, `cargo metadata --locked`, and `cargo audit` (rc=0) all passed; Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock unchanged.
  - **Boundary proof:** Implementation mutates only `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/handshake/mod.rs` (source + its co-located unit test), `docs/ops/IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md`, the NA-0609C evidence doc and testplan, `NEXT_ACTIONS.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `TRACEABILITY.md`, and `docs/ops/ROLLING_OPERATIONS_JOURNAL.md`. No Cargo change; no other source/test; no `.github`/workflow; no canonical spec/input; no `.claude`/guardrail-hook; no qwork/qstart/qresume execution; no sudo/systemd/firewall/Tailnet action; no workflow dispatch/rerun; no branch-protection or repo-settings mutation; no runtime/LAN action.
  - **Ledger:** ENG-0003 closed (done). WF-0004 filed recording the recurring stale qwork-proof-on-existing-checkout issue (observed twice this session) and the drop-before-restart-gate fix plus a recommended runbook note.
  - **Claim boundary:** No endpoint, private port, hostname, topology, token, capability, key, seed, plaintext, ciphertext body, or raw private material is published. No public-readiness, production-readiness, security-completion, crypto-complete, side-channel-free, timing-attack-free, vulnerability-free, or bug-free claim is made; this closes one P3 implementation-attack finding.
  - **Implications for spec/impl/tests:**
    - `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/handshake/mod.rs` gains `hs_ct_eq_32`, uses it at both MAC sites, and carries the co-located equivalence unit test.
    - `docs/governance/evidence/NA-0609C_constant_time_handshake_mac_compare_harness.md` and `tests/NA-0609C_constant_time_handshake_mac_compare_testplan.md` record the change and validation.
    - `docs/ops/IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md` closes ENG-0003 and files WF-0004.
    - `NEXT_ACTIONS.md` inserts NA-0609C IN_PROGRESS while NA-0609 remains the sole READY item.
    - `TRACEABILITY.md` maps NA-0609C to D-1214; the rolling journal records the change.

  - **Date:** 2026-07-06
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** NA-0609D is a read-only re-verification lane executed under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-06-545 (D545), a LITE-CEREMONY lane (single PR, single decision). D-1214 and D-1215 were each consumed once and Accepted; D-1216 was absent before this implementation. The lane corrects a false positive from the NA-0609B audit: ledger ENG-0004 reported the fs_store directory fsync as a no-op, but that no-op is only the `#[cfg(not(unix))]` fallback of `fsync_dir_best_effort`; the `#[cfg(unix)]` variant does the real directory fsync `File::open(dir).and_then(|d| d.sync_all())`. On the x86_64-linux deployment target `write_atomic` performs a full durable-write sequence (content `sync_all` -> atomic `rename` -> directory fsync), so G2 crash-durability is sound; the non-unix no-op is a documented best-effort degradation.
  - **LITE-CEREMONY certification:** The lane reads security-critical code read-only and mutates only docs/evidence/ledger/governance paths; it changes no `.rs`, test, Cargo, workflow, spec, `.claude`, or hook file, applies no source fix, and takes no runtime/LAN action. It therefore qualifies as a read-only LITE-CEREMONY lane per DOC-OPS-006 §9.
  - **Result:** `FS_STORE_DURABILITY_SOUND_ON_UNIX_ENG0004_FALSE_POSITIVE`. Ledger ENG-0004 set to wontfix with the correction; ledger WF-0005 filed (audit-methodology lesson: enumerate and read cfg-gated variants of a symbol for the deployment target before recording a no-op finding); a corrective addendum added to the NA-0609B audit evidence doc. No source was changed because there was nothing to fix.
  - **Boundary proof:** Implementation mutates only `docs/ops/IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md`, `docs/governance/evidence/NA-0609B_qsc_handshake_identity_security_audit_harness.md`, `docs/governance/evidence/NA-0609D_fs_store_durability_reverify_harness.md`, `tests/NA-0609D_fs_store_durability_reverify_testplan.md`, `NEXT_ACTIONS.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `TRACEABILITY.md`, and `docs/ops/ROLLING_OPERATIONS_JOURNAL.md`. - **ID:** D-1224
  - **Title:** NA-0614 mandatory baseline attachment-object padding (size bucketing; crypto/format-adjacent)
  - **Date:** 2026-07-07
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** NA-0614 implements DOC-G5-005 §9 rank 4 / ledger ENG-0010 under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-07-551 (D551): mandatory baseline attachment-object size padding so the stored ciphertext object reveals only a size-ladder bucket to the attachment service/network observer. D-1222 and D-1223 were each consumed once and Accepted; D-1224 was absent before this implementation. The design was locked in DOC-G5-007 before any code; DOC-G5-006's incorrect "client-only, no format change" M1 conclusion was corrected inline. This directive supersedes the NA-0613-queued NA-0614 objective ("client-only, no wire change").
  - **Design (DOC-G5-007):** an additive authenticated `content_len` (true length) is distinct from `plaintext_len` (padded/encrypted length = a ladder bucket), invariant `0 < content_len <= plaintext_len`. The receiver's exact `sum(decrypted) == plaintext_len` integrity check is preserved (now over the padded length) and it additionally truncates the written file to `content_len`. `content_len` is bound in the per-part AAD (`QATT-PART-V1`) and confirm MAC (`QATT-CONFIRM-V1`), so tampering fails AEAD/confirm. The size ladder (powers of two 4 KiB..64 MiB plus a cap bucket == the 100 MiB max) is sender policy; the receiver is ladder-agnostic (honors any valid `content_len`), so the ladder may be retuned in a future build with no format/receiver change. Padding is mandatory (no unpadded path), which eliminates the metadata-downgrade surface by construction pre-release — no negotiation/versioning machinery. `deny_unknown_fields` is retained; `content_len` is a required v1 field and future format changes bump `v` (versioned evolution, not permissive parsing).
  - **Design tenet:** this lane applies the project-wide tenet (excellent architecture + deliberate versioned extension plumbing, without loosening fail-closed strictness; eliminate attack surfaces by construction). The tenet is persisted to the executor's memory and folded into the governance spine by NA-0615.
  - **Change surface:** `store/mod.rs` (record `content_len`, forgiving serde default); `adversarial/payload.rs` (descriptor `content_len`, strict required); `attachments/mod.rs` (ladder + `attachment_pad_to_ladder`; sender zero-fill padding; receiver validation/truncation; AAD/confirm binding; equality predicate); attachment tests updated + new `na0614_padding_tests`. No Cargo/handshake/SCKA/crypto-suite-negotiation/message-plane/workflow/`.claude` change; no new dependency.
  - **Validation:** `cargo fmt --check`/build/clippy/`metadata --locked` green; Cargo unchanged. 38 qsc unit tests pass (incl. 6 new: ladder vectors; `attachment_validate_descriptor` accepts a valid padded descriptor and rejects `content_len == 0` and `content_len > plaintext_len`). Regression suites pass: `attachments_contract_na0217h` (send->pad->upload->fetch->decrypt->truncate round-trip is byte-exact), `adversarial_properties`, `receive_no_mutation`, and the `attachment_streaming_na0197c` forged-descriptor negative (fail-closed reject preserved).
  - **Boundary/claim:** mutates only the attachment source, descriptor struct, attachment tests, DOC-G5-006/007, and the NA-0614 governance artifacts. No handshake/message-plane/crypto-suite change; no runtime/LAN action; no qwork/qstart/qresume. No endpoint, token, capability, key, seed, plaintext, ciphertext body, or raw private material is published. No public-readiness, production-readiness, security-completion, crypto-complete, metadata-free, anonymity, unlinkability, or traffic-analysis-resistant claim is made; padding buckets object size and the honest residual (size range, access existence/timing) remains documented.
  - **Implications for spec/impl/tests:** DOC-G5-007 is the locked format; DOC-G5-006 is corrected; `attachments/mod.rs` ships padding + `content_len`; `na0614_padding_tests` and the updated attachment suites cover it; ENG-0010 is resolved (implemented); ledger/TRACEABILITY/journal updated.
  - **References:** NA-0614; NA-0615; NA-0608; D-1224; D-1223; D-1222; QSL-DIR-2026-07-07-551 (D551); DOC-G5-007; DOC-G5-006; DOC-G5-005; ENG-0010; ENG-0011; `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/attachments/mod.rs`; `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/adversarial/payload.rs`; `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/store/mod.rs`; `docs/design/DOC-G5-007_Attachment_Object_Padding_Format_and_Ladder_v0.1.0_DRAFT.md`; `docs/governance/evidence/NA-0614_attachment_object_padding_harness.md`; `tests/NA-0614_attachment_object_padding_testplan.md`; `docs/ops/IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md`; `TRACEABILITY.md`; `docs/ops/ROLLING_OPERATIONS_JOURNAL.md`

- **ID:** D-1227
  - **Title:** NA-0616 ENG-0001 self-label footgun remediation (fail-closed self-identity selection)
  - **Date:** 2026-07-07
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** NA-0616 remediates ledger ENG-0001 (DOC-G5-005 §9 rank 5) under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-07-553 (D553): the qsc self-identity path silently auto-minted a fresh identity for any `--as <label>` that did not yet exist, so a typo'd/inconsistent self-label operated a divergent identity (peer_mismatch). D-1225 and D-1226 were each consumed once and Accepted; D-1227 was absent before this implementation. The design was locked before code.
  - **Design (design-lock):** a config dir holds one self-identity (`identities/self_<label>.json`); all auto-create call sites are the handshake paths; explicit `identity rotate` creates directly and bypasses the gate; multi-party tests use separate config dirs (no legitimate same-dir multi-identity-via-handshake flow — design-lock STOP not triggered).

First-run auto-create and explicit rotate are preserved. The handshake `--as` default is aligned with `identity show`'s `"self"` (`cmd/mod.rs`). No handshake/SCKA/crypto-suite/wire/state-machine semantic change; no change to identity key derivation/storage/authentication beyond the gate and default; no new dependency.
  - **Validation:** `cargo fmt --check`/build/clippy/`metadata --locked` green; Cargo unchanged. `na_0616_self_label_footgun` (4) passes, incl. an end-to-end proof that a divergent `--as` fails closed with `identity_self_ambiguous` before the network push and mints nothing (no-mutation-on-reject). All qsc unit tests pass (38); no regression across identity_binding, kem_signature_transcript_binding_negative, identity_foundation_contract_na0217d, handshake_contract_na0217i, handshake_security_closure, aws_tui_handshake_na0191, adversarial_properties, identity_secret_at_rest, desktop_gui_contract_na0215b.
  - **Boundary/claim:** mutates only `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/{identity/mod.rs,model/mod.rs,cmd/mod.rs}`, `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/tests/na_0616_self_label_footgun.rs`, the NA-0616 evidence doc/testplan, and governance. No Cargo/handshake/crypto/message-plane/workflow/`.claude` change; no runtime/LAN action; no operator-startup-command execution. No endpoint, token, capability, key, seed, plaintext, ciphertext body, or raw private material is published. No public-readiness, production-readiness, security-completion, crypto-complete, or bug-free claim is made.
  - **Implications for spec/impl/tests:** `identity/mod.rs` fails closed on divergent self-label auto-create; `model/mod.rs` gains `IdentitySelfAmbiguous`; `cmd/mod.rs` defaults handshake `--as` to `"self"`; `na_0616_self_label_footgun` covers it; ENG-0001 resolved; ledger/TRACEABILITY/journal updated.

- **ID:** D-1229
  - **Title:** NA-0617 ENG-0002 attachment single-send-per-session clarification + consumed-session resend fix
  - **Date:** 2026-07-07
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** NA-0617 resolves ledger ENG-0002 (DOC-G5-005 §9 rank 6) under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-07-554 (D554). The ledger asked whether a second `file send` returning `REJECT_QATTSVC_SESSION_STATE` is by design (one attachment per session) or a client limitation. The design-lock showed it is neither once "session" is disambiguated, and substantiated one concrete in-scope client footgun, which this lane fixes under the directive's operator-authorized source carve-out. D-1227 and D-1228 were each consumed once and Accepted; D-1229 was absent before this implementation. The design was locked before code.
  - **Design (design-lock):** two-layer session model — L1 the qsl-attachments SERVICE upload session (single-object BY DESIGN: create → upload → commit → session consumed/removed, object persists; reuse fails closed with `REJECT_QATTSVC_SESSION_STATE`); L2 the qsc CLIENT session (config dir/identity across `file send` invocations, NOT limited to one attachment). The reject is L1 fail-closed behavior on session reuse, not an L2 cap. The footgun: re-sending the SAME file after `ACCEPTED_BY_RELAY` reused the destroyed L1 session (the send-time in-flight guard only catches `PEER_CONFIRMED`/`AWAITING_CONFIRMATION`), surfacing a raw `REJECT_QATTSVC_SESSION_STATE`.
  - **Change:** `attachment_find_outbound_by_source` (`qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/attachments/mod.rs`; sole caller is the send path) now excludes consumed-session states `COMMITTED`/`ACCEPTED_BY_RELAY` (in addition to `PEER_CONFIRMED`) from reuse, so a re-send of an already-delivered file mints a fresh `attachment_id` + fresh encryption context (fresh CEK + nonce prefix) + fresh L1 session and succeeds. Resumable states (`SESSION_CREATED`/`UPLOADING`) and the in-flight state (`AWAITING_CONFIRMATION`) remain reusable, preserving resume and in-flight blocking. Client-side attachment journal reuse logic only.
  - **Security invariants introduced/changed:** L1 single-object-per-session invariant is preserved. No nonce reuse (each fresh record derives a new CEK + nonce prefix). No protocol/wire/crypto/state-machine (SCKA/ratchet) change; no attachment wire/descriptor/object/padding format change. A previously-unrecoverable `COMMITTED`-but-relay-send-failed transfer now re-sends cleanly (fail-closed → fresh session). Behavior change is a reject→success for a legitimate re-send whose prior reject was an accidental dead-session reuse, not a deliberate control.
  - **Validation:** `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo build -p qsc --locked` and `cargo metadata --locked` green; Cargo.toml/lock unchanged (advisories posture identical to main). `na_0617_attachment_single_send_per_session` (4/4) passes: distinct multi-send succeeds; same-file resend now succeeds without `REJECT_QATTSVC_SESSION_STATE`; interrupted upload resumes and commits; resend while awaiting confirmation is blocked (`attachment_send_inflight`). Negative control (class-only): with the predicate reverted to `PEER_CONFIRMED`-only the resend test fails with `code=REJECT_QATTSVC_SESSION_STATE`. Regression: `attachment_streaming_na0197c` (17 pass, 1 local-only ignored) incl. `attachment_upload_resume_and_invalid_resume_token_fail_closed` (guards `UPLOADING` reuse) and `attachment_e2e_resume_and_peer_confirm_after_persistence`. Changed lib + new test are clippy-clean (`--lib` / `--test` under `-D warnings`).
  - **Boundary/claim:** mutates only `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/attachments/mod.rs`, `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/tests/na_0617_attachment_single_send_per_session.rs`, the NA-0617 evidence doc/testplan, and governance. No qsl-attachments/qsl-server change; no Cargo/handshake/crypto/message-plane/attachment-format/workflow/`.claude` change; no runtime/LAN action; no operator-startup-command execution. No endpoint, token, capability, key, seed, plaintext, ciphertext body, or raw private material is published. - **ID:** D-1232
  - **Title:** NA-0618 ENG-0013 Suite-2 symmetric counter overflow hard-stop
  - **Date:** 2026-07-07
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** NA-0618 implements ledger ENG-0013 (Comprehensive/Suite-2 review H-1) under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-07-555 (D555): the Suite-2 symmetric message counters `ns`/`nr` advanced with `saturating_add(1)` and no `u32::MAX` hard-stop. Since Suite-2 sessions never re-key (ENG-0012), a saturated counter with static header keys would repeat a header nonce/ciphertext (nonce-reuse class, bounded behind ~4.29e9 one-way messages). D-1230 and D-1231 were each consumed once and Accepted; D-1232 was absent before this implementation. The design was locked before code.
  - **Design (design-lock):** three counter-advance sites in `tools/refimpl/quantumshield_refimpl/src/suite2/ratchet.rs` — `send_wire` (`ns`), `recv_nonboundary_ooo` (`nr`), `recv_boundary_in_order` (`nr`). The recv reject paths return unmutated `state: st`; the receive-side overflow is unreachable through the public API because a compliant `send_wire` never originates a message at the saturating counter (defense-in-depth only). Mirrors the sibling `qsp` module's `ns == u32::MAX` guard.
  - **Change:** added `checked_counter_inc(counter: u32) -> Result<u32, &'static str>` (fail-closed `+1` returning `REJECT_S2_COUNTER_OVERFLOW` when it would pass `u32::MAX`), used at all three advance sites in place of `saturating_add`. `send_wire` computes `ns_next` and fails closed BEFORE deriving key material; the recv paths compute `nr_next` and, on `Err`, return their outcome with `reason = REJECT_S2_COUNTER_OVERFLOW` and no state mutation. Added the `REJECT_S2_COUNTER_OVERFLOW` reject const (local reason code, pattern of `REJECT_S2_CHAINKEY_UNSET`) and registered it in `DOC-CAN-003 §10` for G4 spec/impl parity.
  - **Security invariants introduced/changed:** the send and receive paths now terminate (fail closed) when a symmetric counter would pass `u32::MAX`, closing a bounded nonce-reuse edge; no-mutation-on-reject holds at all three sites. `REJECT_S2_COUNTER_OVERFLOW` is a LOCAL reason code (not wire-transmitted; consistent with the NA-0612 finding). No key-schedule/KDF/AEAD/nonce-derivation/wire-format/descriptor change. This does NOT implement the DH ratchet / PQ reseed (ENG-0012) and makes no post-compromise or Triple-Ratchet claim.
  - **Validation:** `checked_counter_inc_boundary_and_normal` (0→Ok(1), MAX-1→Ok(MAX), MAX→Err) and `send_wire_rejects_counter_overflow_at_ns_max_and_no_mutation` (reject + deterministic + no mutation + no AEAD use) pass; the receive-side guards use the same helper. Full `quantumshield_refimpl` suite green (70 lib + all integration; 0 failures). `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p quantumshield_refimpl --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `cargo build -p quantumshield_refimpl` and `cargo metadata --locked` green; Cargo.toml/lock unchanged (advisories posture identical to main). suite2 conformance vectors use small counters and are unaffected.
  - **Boundary/claim:** mutates only `tools/refimpl/quantumshield_refimpl/src/suite2/ratchet.rs`, `docs/canonical/DOC-CAN-003_QSP_Suite-2_True_Triple_Ratchet_v5.0.0_DRAFT.md` (one reject-code registration), the NA-0618 evidence doc/testplan, and governance. No qsc-client/qsl-attachments/qsl-server change; no other refimpl module; no Cargo/workflow/`.claude`/hook change; no runtime/LAN action; no operator-startup-command execution. No endpoint, token, capability, key, seed, plaintext, ciphertext body, or raw private material is published. No public-readiness, production-readiness, security-completion, crypto-complete, or bug-free claim is introduced.
  - **Implications for spec/impl/tests:** `suite2/ratchet.rs` fails closed at counter saturation via `checked_counter_inc`; `DOC-CAN-003 §10` registers `REJECT_S2_COUNTER_OVERFLOW`; the two new unit tests cover it; ENG-0013 resolved; ledger/TRACEABILITY/journal updated.
  - **References:** NA-0618; D-1232; D-1231; D-1230; QSL-DIR-2026-07-07-555 (D555); ENG-0013; ENG-0012; qsp/ratchet.rs (reference guard); `tools/refimpl/quantumshield_refimpl/src/suite2/ratchet.rs`; `docs/canonical/DOC-CAN-003_QSP_Suite-2_True_Triple_Ratchet_v5.0.0_DRAFT.md`; `docs/governance/evidence/NA-0618_suite2_counter_overflow_hardstop_harness.md`; `tests/NA-0618_suite2_counter_overflow_hardstop_testplan.md`; `docs/ops/IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md`; `TRACEABILITY.md`; `docs/ops/ROLLING_OPERATIONS_JOURNAL.md`

  - **Title:** NA-0619 ENG-0012 send-side ratchet liveness feasibility + design (DOC-G5-008); NA-0620 restoration
  - **Date:** 2026-07-07
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** NA-0619 (docs-only, LITE-CEREMONY single PR) under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-08-556 (D556) produces `docs/design/DOC-G5-008` — the feasibility + staged design for making the Suite-2 ratchet re-key on the real client send path (ledger ENG-0012, the P1 that blocks the G1/G2 release gates). It designs; it implements nothing and changes no source and makes no normative spec change. D-1232 and D-1233 were each consumed once and Accepted; D-1234 was absent before this lane.
  - **Design study (read-only, confirmed at `8d9b158e`):** C-1 (zero X25519 in suite2; `Suite2SendState`/`Suite2RecvState` carry a fixed `dh_pub` nonce input and have no X25519 private key, no `DHr`, no live `RK`); C-2 (`send_wire` rejects nonzero flags; no `send_boundary`/`send_pq_ctxt`; the receive side `recv_boundary_in_order`/`apply_pq_reseed` is complete but unreachable); the static-`rk` bootstrap (`qsp_activate_*_chain_if_needed`); and that `suite2/parse.rs` permits a bare `FLAG_BOUNDARY` (DH-only boundary) — correcting the audit's imprecise "parse requires FLAG_PQ_CTXT whenever FLAG_BOUNDARY is set". Feasibility rests on the existing receiver machinery, the `qsp::dh_ratchet_send` reference, and the complete DOC-CAN-003 §8.5 spec.
  - **What DOC-G5-008 specifies:** ten sections — problem + code-grounded proof; feasibility; trigger policy (ratchet-on-reply + bounded count/time fallback; sparse PQ reseed); DH-only vs co-scheduled boundaries; sender construction (`send_boundary`/`send_pq_ctxt` mirroring the receiver + qsp reference) and the required state additions (DH keypair, `DHr`, live `RK`); qsc wiring (remove the static-`rk` bootstrap; crash-safe persistence, G2); conformance-vector requirements (both ratchets firing mid-session through the real send path; a PCS-healing vector); the counter-hard-stop interaction (a live ratchet resets `Ns:=0`, mooting the ENG-0013 precondition); a staged three-lane implementation plan; open questions for operator decision; and a G5 traffic-shape note. Binding claim boundary: no Triple-Ratchet / post-compromise / quantum-secure claim until Stages 1–2 land and vectors pass.

- **ID:** D-1235
  - **Title:** NA-0620 ENG-0012 Stage 1a: Suite-2 DH-ratchet state plumbing (no behavior change)
  - **Date:** 2026-07-08
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** NA-0620 implements Stage 1a of the accepted design DOC-G5-008 (ledger ENG-0012, the P1 blocking the G1/G2 release gates) under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-08-557 (D557): make the Suite-2 session state able to carry and persist the DH-ratchet material the Stage-1b send-side ratchet needs, with NO message-path behavior change. The operator elected to sub-stage (plumbing then behavior) and to use a reply-driven + bounded-fallback DH trigger in Stage 1b. D-1233 and D-1234 were each consumed once and Accepted; D-1235 was absent before this implementation. The design was locked before code.
  - **Design (design-lock):** the DH keypair material already existed and partly flowed (the qsc handshake retains `dh_sk`; `init_from_base_handshake` already accepted the DH pubs and computed `rk`); the ratchet state lacked the local DH private key, `DHr`, and a session-level live `RK`. The crash-restart conformance vector is operational (runtime-captured snapshot bytes), not byte-pinned, so a snapshot version bump is transparent — a clean no-behavior-change plumbing is achievable (directive STOP not triggered).
  - **Change:** added a session-level `Suite2DhRatchetState { dhs_priv, dhs_pub, dhr, rk }` as a `dh` field on `Suite2SessionState`; `establish.rs` populates `dhs_pub`/`dhr`/`rk` (leaving `dhs_priv` zero for non-ratcheting callers) with `init_from_base_handshake`'s signature UNCHANGED (so the interop actor and handshake tests are untouched); `Suite2SessionState::set_dh_self_priv` lets the qsc handshake thread its retained X25519 ephemeral private key (`hs_build_session` gains a param; the initiator converts `pending.dh_sk` fail-closed on length); the snapshot format is bumped to v2 (DH state serialized after `mkskipped`; restore accepts v2 only and fails closed on any other version — pre-release, eliminate legacy). The seed-fallback session derives its DH material from the existing seed labels plus `QSC.QSP.DH.PRIV`.
  - **Security invariants introduced/changed:** NONE to the message path. No `send_wire`/`recv_wire`/nonce/header/wire-byte change (the runtime-equivalence test confirms the persisted state matches the refimpl byte-for-byte); the static-`rk` bootstrap is untouched (removed in Stage 1b); no `send_boundary`; no KDF/AEAD/primitive change. `dhs_priv`/`rk` are secrets persisted only through the vault-encrypted snapshot, consistent with the existing `ck_ec`/`ck_pq` posture. This lane delivers no post-compromise security on its own.
  - **Validation:** new `snapshot_roundtrip_preserves_dh_ratchet_state` and `restore_rejects_non_v2_version` unit tests pass. Full `quantumshield_refimpl` suite green (72 lib + all integration, incl. na_0300/na_0243/na_0301). The touched qsc suites pass — `session_state_at_rest`, `protocol_state_contract_na0217c`, `qsp_qse_onwire`, `suite2_runtime_equivalence_na0198` (no message-path drift), and the handshake suites (`handshake_mvp`, `handshake_security_closure`, `na_0304`, `na_0313`) exercising the threaded DH private key. `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy` (refimpl all-targets + qsc lib) `-D warnings` clean; `cargo metadata --locked` green; Cargo.toml/lock unchanged.

- **ID:** D-1237
  - **Title:** NA-0621 — ENG-0012 Stage 1b-i: Suite-2 DH ratchet (send+receive) + NHK header keys, refimpl core
  - **Date:** 2026-07-08
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** Implement the classical X25519 DH ratchet for Suite-2 IN REFIMPL ONLY, under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-08-558 (D558), per DOC-CAN-003 §3.3.2/§3.4/§8.1/§8.5.1/§8.5.2. Adds `KDF_RK_DH`, the on-demand `HK/NHK` header-key derivation, `send_boundary` (DH-ratchet send), and `recv_dh_boundary` (DH-ratchet receive + §8.5.1 CURRENT_NHK anti-spoof), advancing ENG-0012 to Stage-1b-i-done. Does NOT wire the qsc client, does NOT remove the static-`rk` bootstrap (Stage 1b-ii = NA-0622), and does NOT touch the PQ-reseed sender (Stage 2). The P1 stays OPEN until Stage 1b-ii wires the ratchet into the real qsc send path.
  - **Design-lock (STOP condition NOT triggered):** a clean, spec-faithful implementation is achievable with no wire-format change, no non-boundary-path change, and no PQ-reseed-semantics change. Established at `1ec1784f`: (a) `DH_pub[32]` is already on the wire per §4.3 (`parse_ratchet_header` extracts it, `send_wire` writes it) — the current code merely uses the stored `dh_pub` instead of ratcheting on it, so the DH ratchet is a behavior change, not a format change; (b) the classical DH ratchet was absent on BOTH sides (`recv_boundary_in_order` does only the PQ reseed, 0 X25519/`kdf_rk_dh`/keypair uses); (c) Suite-2 had no `NHK` at all, which §8.5.1's anti-spoof requires — `NHK` is derived on demand from `RK`, so no stored field and no snapshot change; (d) a DH-only boundary needs its own path because `parse_pq_prefix` requires `FLAG_PQ_CTXT`.
  - **Derivations:** `KDF_RK_DH = KMAC256(RK,"QSP5.0/RKDH",dh_out,64) -> (RK'||CK_ec0)`; `HK/NHK_{A->B,B->A} = KMAC32(RK,"QSP5.0/{HK,NHK}/{dir}",[0x01])` mapped to send/recv by role. `send_boundary`: `boundary_hk = NHK_s(pre-boundary RK)`, fresh X25519 keypair, `dh_out = X25519(new_priv, DHr)`, `KDF_RK_DH`, reinit `CK_pq_send`, recompute `HK_s`, `PN:=Ns`, `Ns:=0`, `FLAG_BOUNDARY` with new `DH_pub`, header under `boundary_hk`. `recv_dh_boundary`: header MUST decrypt under CURRENT `NHK_r` (else reject), then `dh_out = X25519(DHs_priv, msg.DH_pub)`, `KDF_RK_DH`, reinit `CK_pq_recv`, recompute `HK_r`, `DHr:=msg.DH_pub`, `Nr:=0`, decrypt body; commit only on full success (no mutation on reject). The send chain is CREATED by the ratchet so the responder can send (this is the gap the static-`rk` bootstrap fills today; removed in 1b-ii).
  - **Proof:** co-located refimpl conformance tests pass — `dh_ratchet_two_party_roundtrip_both_directions` (the ratchet fires both directions and messages decrypt), `dh_ratchet_pcs_healing` (a pre-ratchet epoch-0 state snapshot cannot decrypt post-ratchet messages once both parties advanced — post-compromise self-healing), and `dh_ratchet_no_mutation_on_reject`. The full `quantumshield_refimpl` suite (75 lib + integration) stays green (non-boundary and PQ-reseed paths unchanged); `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`, `fmt --check`, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, and `metadata --locked` are clean; Cargo unchanged.
  - **Boundary/claim:** mutates only `tools/refimpl/quantumshield_refimpl/src/suite2/ratchet.rs` (DH ratchet + NHK + tests) and governance/design docs (`docs/design/DOC-G5-008_*` correction; `docs/ops/IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md`; evidence + testplan; `DECISIONS.md`; `TRACEABILITY.md`; `docs/ops/ROLLING_OPERATIONS_JOURNAL.md`; `NEXT_ACTIONS.md`). No qsc client change; no static-`rk` removal; no PQ-reseed (`apply_pq_reseed`) change; no KDF/AEAD primitive change; no normative DOC-CAN change; no wire-format change; no snapshot change; no Cargo/`.github`/`.claude`/hook change; no operator-startup-command execution; no runtime/LAN action. Research/demo only. This lane delivers the DH-ratchet crypto core in refimpl; it is NOT wired into the client and is NOT on its own a post-compromise, Triple-Ratchet, security-completion, crypto-complete, or production-readiness claim. No endpoint, token, capability, key, seed, plaintext, ciphertext body, or raw private material is published.
  - **Implications for spec/impl/tests:** ENG-0012 advances to Stage-1b-i-done; the DH ratchet send+receive + NHK exist and are proven in refimpl (incl. PCS self-healing); DOC-G5-008 §2 is corrected for the NHK/receive-DH gap. Remaining: Stage 1b-ii (NA-0622: qsc trigger wiring + static-`rk` removal + end-to-end qsc two-party/PCS vectors; resolves the trigger-defaults open question) and Stage 2 (PQ reseed). Closeout is D-1238; the successor begins at D-1239.
  - **References:** NA-0621; D-1237; D-1238; QSL-DIR-2026-07-08-558 (D558); ENG-0012; DOC-G5-008; DOC-CAN-003 §3.3.2/§3.4/§8.1/§8.5.1/§8.5.2/§4.3; WF-0013; qsl-protocol main `1ec1784f`; `tools/refimpl/quantumshield_refimpl/src/suite2/ratchet.rs`; `docs/governance/evidence/NA-0621_dh_ratchet_refimpl_core_harness.md`; `tests/NA-0621_dh_ratchet_refimpl_core_testplan.md`

- **ID:** D-1239
  - **Title:** NA-0622 — ENG-0012 Stage 1b-ii: qsc DH-ratchet trigger + static-rk removal (classical DH ratchet on the real send path)
  - **Date:** 2026-07-08
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** Wire the classical X25519 DH ratchet into the REAL qsc send/receive path under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-08-559 (D559), building on the Stage-1b-i refimpl core (NA-0621, D-1237). `qsp_pack` originates a DH boundary via the refimpl `send_boundary` when the trigger fires (else `send_wire_canon`); `qsp_unpack` routes an incoming DH-only boundary to `recv_dh_boundary`. The static-`rk` bootstrap (`qsp_activate_responder_send_chain_if_needed`, `qsp_activate_initiator_recv_chain_if_needed`) is REMOVED — ratchet-on-reply now creates the responder's send chain and the initiator's recv chain. This CLOSES the CLASSICAL half of the P1 (ENG-0012): classical post-compromise security now runs on live qsc traffic. Stage 2 (the PQ-reseed sender = NA-0623) remains for full post-quantum PCS.
  - **Operator decisions (locked in D559):** TRIGGER = RATCHET-ON-REPLY (a `pending` bit set on every receive; the first send after any receive is a DH boundary) + a bounded fallback of N_dh=4 messages / T_dh=15 min (operator delegated the N=4-vs-8 choice; executor set N=4 — halves the worst-case burst exposure window at marginal cost, well clear of the always-ratchet N=1 loss-fragility cliff). METADATA = ACCEPT + DOCUMENT: the DH-boundary observable (FLAG_BOUNDARY + a fresh on-wire DH_pub, reply-correlated) is recorded in DOC-G5-004; cover-traffic obfuscation is deferred to ENG-0022 (filed here), sequenced after Stage 2.
  - **Persistence (qsc session-blob v2):** qsc is load-per-message (no in-memory session cache), so the reply-driven trigger MUST be persisted. The trigger (`pending` + `msgs_since_ratchet` + `last_ratchet_unix_secs`, 13 bytes) is carried inside the encrypted session-blob plaintext as `b"QTRG"` + trigger + QS2S snapshot (v2); legacy raw-snapshot plaintexts migrate transparently (default trigger). `qsp_session_store` keeps its signature (18 call sites untouched) and PRESERVES the on-disk trigger; the message path uses `qsp_session_store_with_trigger`. The refimpl `Suite2SessionState` / QS2S snapshot is FROZEN (no snapshot bump); no blob-envelope-format change; no wire-format change (DH_pub is already on the wire per §4.3).
  - **Seed-fallback gate (session-based, test-only):** the DH ratchet is gated OFF for a DEGENERATE SELF-DH session (`st.dh.dhr == st.dh.dhs_pub`) — the unsafe seed-fallback TEST model, a SYMMETRIC (both role-A) session that cannot round-trip the direction-sensitive DH ratchet (sender signs a boundary header under NHK_A->B while a role-A receiver would try NHK_B->A). The gate keys off the SESSION STATE, not the `allow_unsafe_seed_fallback_for_tests()` flag, because real-handshake tests also set that flag (it merely PERMITS seed fallback) and a real session MUST ratchet even with the flag set (its responder send chain is unset once the static-`rk` bootstrap is gone). Real, handshake-established sessions have `dhr != dhs` and always ratchet; the seed model (`dhr == dhs`) never occurs in production, so the pre-existing seed-model regression suite stays byte-for-byte green while real-handshake suites (same_host, send_ready_markers, na_030x) exercise the live ratchet.
  - **Proof (end-to-end over a REAL A/B handshake):** `dh_ratchet_e2e_roundtrip_over_real_handshake` (Alice initiator/role A, Bob responder/role B: Alice's first send is normal, Bob's reply is a DH boundary via ratchet-on-reply that creates his send chain, Alice processes the boundary and decrypts, and the reverse direction ratchets too) and `dh_ratchet_e2e_pcs_healing_over_real_handshake` (a restored pre-ratchet session snapshot cannot decrypt a post-ratchet message — post-compromise self-healing on the real client). The runtime-equivalence test stays byte-for-byte equivalent to the refimpl (seed path, gated); the full qsc suite (attachment/message/transport/relay/handshake/session-at-rest) is green; the refimpl suite is unchanged (frozen). `cargo build --workspace --all-targets` (WF-0013), `fmt --check`, `clippy -p qsc --lib`/changed-test-targets `-D warnings`, and `metadata --locked` are clean; Cargo unchanged.
  - **Boundary/claim:** mutates only `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/**`, qsc tests (e2e vectors + a v2-strip helper fix + one pre-existing `== false` clippy fix in an allowed test path), and governance/design docs (DOC-G5-004, DOC-G5-008, IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER incl. ENG-0022 + ENG-0012 Stage-1b-ii-done; evidence + testplan; DECISIONS; TRACEABILITY; journal; NEXT_ACTIONS). No refimpl change; no PQ-reseed (`apply_pq_reseed`) change; no KDF/AEAD primitive change; no wire-format change; no normative DOC-CAN change; no Cargo/`.github`/`.claude`/hook change; no operator-startup-command execution; no runtime/LAN action. Research/demo only. The CLASSICAL half of the P1 is closed; this is NOT a post-quantum, Triple-Ratchet, security-completion, crypto-complete, or production-readiness claim (the post-quantum guarantee awaits Stage 2). No endpoint, token, capability, key, seed, plaintext, ciphertext body, or raw private material is published.

- **ID:** D-1241
  - **Title:** NA-0623 — ENG-0012 Stage 2a: Suite-2 SCKA sender core (advertisement + PQ reseed) + both-sides RK advance
  - **Date:** 2026-07-08
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** Implement the Suite-2 SCKA sender core IN REFIMPL ONLY under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-08-560 (D560), per DOC-CAN-004 §3.1–§3.4 and DOC-CAN-003 §8.5.3/§8.5.4/§3.3.3/§3.3.6. Adds `KDF_RK_PQ`; the SCKA advertisement sender (`send_pq_advertise`), peer-advertisement monotonicity tracking (`track_peer_adv`), and the PQ-reseed sender (`send_pq_reseed`); and — per the D560 AMENDMENT — the both-sides ROOT ADVANCE: the receiver (`recv_boundary_in_order`) now advances `RK := KDF_RK_PQ(RK_old, pq_epoch_ss)` and recomputes `HK_r` after `apply_pq_reseed`, and the new sender mirrors it, so the PQ epoch secret lands in the root and the classical DH ratchet carries it forward permanently. The advertised-key store and the ML-KEM KeyGen/Encap are CALLER-side (the refimpl SCKA sender is pure functions). Advances ENG-0012 to Stage-2a-done. Does NOT wire the qsc client (Stage 2b = NA-0624); does NOT change `apply_pq_reseed`'s SCKA CTXT-validation semantics; no KDF/AEAD/KEM primitive change; no normative DOC-CAN change; no snapshot or wire-format change. The P1 stays OPEN until Stage 2b delivers post-quantum PCS on the real qsc send path.
  - **Amendment / security re-scope (D560, operator-approved):** the Phase-2 design-lock found the existing PQ-reseed receiver (`recv_boundary_in_order` -> `apply_pq_reseed`) absorbs `pq_epoch_ss` into the directional PQ chains but NEVER advances the root `RK` (DOC-CAN-003 §8.5.3 steps 5+7 unimplemented). Because the classical DH ratchet (`send_boundary`/`recv_dh_boundary`, NA-0621) reinitialises `CK_pq` from `RK` (§8.5.2 step 6), the next DH reply would WIPE the post-quantum hardening. Operator decision: FIX BOTH SIDES — add `KDF_RK_PQ` + `HK` recompute to the receiver AND the new sender. The `apply_pq_reseed` CTXT-validation semantics (monotonicity/one-time/tombstone/target/ct-len) remain unchanged.
  - **Design-lock (STOP condition NOT triggered):** a clean, spec-faithful implementation is achievable with NO snapshot bump, NO non-boundary-path change, and NO wire-format change. The SCKA target sets (`known/consumed/tombstoned_targets`, `peer_max_adv_id_seen`) already exist and persist (snapshot v2); the KEM key material is caller-side (`apply_pq_reseed` takes `pq_epoch_ss` as an input, so the sender is pure functions and `local_next_adv_id`/`advkeys` live in the caller); `parse.rs` already parses `FLAG_PQ_ADV`/`FLAG_PQ_CTXT` (both require `FLAG_BOUNDARY`), so the sender constructs the existing format. DOC-CAN-003 §8.1 defines ONE `RK` per session; the refimpl stores it in both `recv.rk` (the PQ path) and `dh.rk` (the DH ratchet), and the reseed writes the advanced root to BOTH slots so the DH ratchet carries the PQ hardening. `send_pq_advertise` records the advertised id in `known_targets` so a later peer CTXT targeting it passes the receiver's known-target check.
  - **Derivations:** `KDF_RK_PQ = KMAC32(RK,"QSP5.0/RKPQ",pq_ss||[0x01])` (§3.3.3 — the same derivation `establish` uses for the initial PQ mix-in). The `KDF_PQ_RESEED` directional seeds are REUSED from `apply_pq_reseed` (factored into a shared `kdf_pq_reseed_seeds` helper; `apply_pq_reseed`'s output is byte-identical) so both parties converge. §3.3.6 normative ordering (CAT-S2-KDF-001): seeds from `RK_old` FIRST, then `RK := KDF_RK_PQ`, then apply the directional `CK_pq`. `send_pq_reseed` mirrors `recv_boundary_in_order`'s PQ path: seeds from `RK_old`, advance `RK`, recompute `HK_s`/`HK_r`, replace `CK_pq_send`/`CK_pq_recv`, frame `FLAG_PQ_CTXT|FLAG_BOUNDARY` (`pq_prefix = pq_target_id || pq_ct`) under the PRE-reseed key schedule. `send_pq_advertise` frames `FLAG_PQ_ADV|FLAG_BOUNDARY` (`pq_adv_id || pq_adv_pub`).
  - **Refimpl-vs-spec note (flagged, not fixed):** the frozen CTXT receiver (`recv_boundary_in_order`) opens the PQ-CTXT boundary header under the ordinary `HK_r`, not the §8.5.1 `NHK`; the sender mirrors `HK_s` so the round-trip holds. Reconciling the PQ-CTXT boundary header to the §8.5.1 `NHK` anti-spoof rule would change the frozen receiver's semantics (out of scope here) — recorded for the Stage-2b / a spec-alignment lane.
  - **Proof:** co-located refimpl integration tests (`tools/refimpl/quantumshield_refimpl/tests/suite2_scka_sender.rs`): `reseed_round_trip_sender_to_apply_pq_reseed_decrypts_and_converges` (advertise -> encapsulate -> the frozen `apply_pq_reseed` path decrypts; the directional PQ seed and the advanced root converge on both parties); `pq_pcs_healing_survives_dh_ratchet` (THE HEADLINE — a state snapshot captured BEFORE a PQ reseed CANNOT open the post-reseed classical DH boundary, while the live receiver can: the PQ epoch secret advanced the root the DH ratchet reads and is carried forward permanently); `reseed_sender_rejects_are_deterministic_and_no_mutation`, `reseed_replay_is_rejected_one_time`, `advertise_frames_parseable_boundary_and_track_enforces_monotonicity` (fail-closed rejects, one-time consumption, peer-ADV monotonicity, no state mutation). Harness ops `suite2.send_pq_advertise`/`suite2.send_pq_reseed` drive 6 byte-pinned CAT-SCKA-LOGIC-001 conformance vectors (append-only; the existing 8 vectors are byte-identical). The frozen `apply_pq_reseed` (pqreseed 5/5), boundary (4/4), SCKA-KEM (5/5), and KDF (6/6) vectors stay UNCHANGED green; the full `quantumshield_refimpl` suite (75 lib + integration) is green; the vector schema validates. `cargo build --workspace --all-targets` (WF-0013), `fmt --check`, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on the changed crates, and `metadata --locked` are clean; Cargo unchanged.
  - **Boundary/claim:** mutates only `tools/refimpl/quantumshield_refimpl/src/suite2/ratchet.rs` (KDF_RK_PQ + receiver RK-advance + recv_wire propagation + the SCKA sender), `tools/refimpl/quantumshield_refimpl/src/suite2/scka.rs` (extracted shared seed helper; `apply_pq_reseed` byte-identical), `tools/refimpl/quantumshield_refimpl/tests/suite2_scka_sender.rs` (new), `tools/actors/refimpl_actor_rs/src/main.rs` (two SCKA sender ops), `inputs/suite2/vectors/qshield_suite2_scka_logic_vectors_v1.json` (+6 vectors, append-only), and governance/design docs (`docs/design/DOC-G5-008_*`; `docs/ops/IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md`; evidence + testplan; `DECISIONS.md`; `TRACEABILITY.md`; `docs/ops/ROLLING_OPERATIONS_JOURNAL.md`). No qsc client change; no `apply_pq_reseed` CTXT-validation-semantic change; no KDF/AEAD/KEM primitive change; no normative DOC-CAN change; no snapshot or wire-format change; no Cargo/`.github`/`.claude`/hook change; no operator-startup-command execution; no runtime/LAN action. Research/demo only. This lane delivers the SCKA sender core + both-sides root advance in refimpl (incl. PQ-PCS surviving a DH ratchet); it is NOT wired into the client and is NOT on its own a post-quantum, Triple-Ratchet, security-completion, crypto-complete, post-compromise, or production-readiness claim (the post-quantum guarantee on live traffic awaits Stage 2b). No endpoint, token, capability, key, seed, plaintext, ciphertext body, or raw private material is published.
  - **Implications for spec/impl/tests:** ENG-0012 advances to Stage-2a-done; the SCKA advertisement + PQ-reseed sender and the both-sides RK advance exist and are proven in refimpl (incl. the headline PQ-PCS-survives-a-DH-ratchet property). Remaining: Stage 2b (NA-0624 — wire the SCKA advertisement + reseed cadence into the real qsc send path, persist the SCKA state, add end-to-end qsc vectors), which delivers post-quantum forward secrecy on live traffic and FULLY closes the P1. Closeout is D-1242; the successor begins at D-1243.

- **ID:** D-1243
  - **Title:** NA-0624 — ENG-0012 Stage 2b: qsc SCKA wiring (advertise + reseed cadence + persistence); the P1 CLOSES
  - **Date:** 2026-07-08
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5
  - **Decision:** Wire the Stage-2a (NA-0623, D-1241) SCKA sender into the REAL qsc send/receive path under directive QSL-DIR-2026-07-08-561 (D561), REUSING the frozen refimpl semantics exactly (`send_pq_advertise`/`send_pq_reseed`/`track_peer_adv`/`apply_pq_reseed` unchanged; additive qsc-side wiring only; the seed-model runtime-equivalence test stays byte-for-byte). (1) ADVERTISE: `qsp_pack` originates SCKA advertisements as separate CONTROL envelopes pushed before the main message (the frozen receiver has no ADV body decrypt path — a control envelope carries no application payload and the peer's OOO machinery skips its chain step); the ML-KEM-768 receive keypair is generated caller-side and the secret persisted FAIL-CLOSED before the advertisement wire can leave `qsp_pack`. (2) TRACK: `qsp_unpack` intercepts `FLAG_PQ_ADV` BEFORE `recv_wire` (which rejects it), validates via the frozen `track_peer_adv` (length + monotonicity), and persists the peer advertisement. (3) RESEED SEND: on the approved cadence `qsp_pack` encapsulates to the peer's advertised key and originates the `FLAG_PQ_CTXT` boundary via the frozen `send_pq_reseed` (which already writes the advanced root to both root slots); the consumed peer advertisement persists fail-closed before the wire exists (a crash may never re-target a consumed advertisement). (4) RESEED RECEIVE: `qsp_unpack` routes `FLAG_PQ_CTXT` by looking up the targeted local advertised key, decapsulating, INJECTING the canonical session root into the receive state (`recv.rk := dh.rk` when live — a DH boundary advances only `dh.rk`, and the frozen reseed SENDER derives from `session_root`, so the receiver must mirror it or the parties derive `KDF_RK_PQ` from different roots; the NA-0623 dh.rk-sync carry-over, resolved caller-side), driving the frozen `apply_pq_reseed` via `recv_wire(..., Some(pq_epoch_ss), Some(pq_target_id))`, and then ADOPTING the advanced root into the DH-ratchet slot (`dh.rk := recv.rk`) — the caller-side composition Stage 2a deferred to qsc, so a later classical DH ratchet CARRIES the PQ hardening instead of wiping it; the consumed local key is erased (one-time) before the plaintext is released. (5) PERSIST: the SCKA state — a bounded advertised-key store (CAP=4, deterministic lowest-id eviction, consumed-first), the peer advertisement, `local_next_adv_id`, `peer_adv_max_seen`, and the cadence counters — persists INSIDE the AEAD session blob as a length-delimited v3 plaintext section (`QTRG(4) + trigger(13) + scka_len(u32 LE) + scka + QS2S`); the refimpl QS2S snapshot stays FROZEN; legacy v2/v1 blobs migrate transparently; ML-KEM secret keys exist only inside the encrypted blob; the codec is fail-closed (exact-length, hard caps). G2 rollback: a monotonic side-record (ids only — `peer_max_adv_id_seen`, `local_next_adv_id`, `peer_adv_max_seen`, `peer_adv_consumed_max` (a rolled-back store must never re-consume a one-time peer target), tombstones; the qsc mirror of the actor `dur_scka` record) is merge-updated on every store and checked on every load — a rolled-back v3 blob FAILS CLOSED (`session_rollback_detected`). ADV/reseed pack exclusion: an advertisement consumes a send-chain slot the receiver skips as a control message — a NORMAL main message heals the receiver's n-gap via the OOO machinery and a DH boundary abandons the old epoch, but the frozen reseed receiver is strict-in-order, so an advertisement NEVER shares a pack with a reseed (it defers to the next send). Closes ENG-0012 (the P1): post-quantum forward secrecy now runs on live qsc traffic.
  - **Cadence (Operator Decision 3, defaults pinned at design-lock):** advertise on establishment (first send with a live chain), when the local advertised key is consumed, and on rotation (T_pq); reseed when a fresh unconsumed peer advertisement is available AND sparsely — the first reseed immediately, thereafter every N_pq=8 sent DH boundaries or T_pq=3600 s — evaluated on non-DH-boundary sends so reseeds co-schedule after DH boundaries. Rationale: reseeds are ~2x sparser than the DH fallback cadence in message count and hour-scale in time (the KEM ciphertext is ~1088 B); rotation heals lost advertisements/reseeds (which otherwise degrade to the classical status quo). The SCKA path is gated OFF for the degenerate self-DH seed session (`dhr == dhs`), exactly like the DH ratchet, keeping the seed-model runtime-equivalence byte-for-byte (`scka_len == 0`).
  - **Operator decisions (all approved 2026-07-08, D561):** (1) PQ-only reseed reusing Stage 2a exactly — the combined DH+PQ boundary needs a new refimpl receiver and is filed as a future refimpl lane; (2) persistence = session-blob v3 (not a separate store); (3) cadence as above; (4) metadata ACCEPT + DOCUMENT — the `FLAG_PQ_ADV` (~1184 B) / `FLAG_PQ_CTXT` (~1088 B) wire observables are documented in DOC-G5-004 §3.1, cover traffic stays deferred (ENG-0022); (5) NHK-vs-HK DEFERRED to a dedicated spec-alignment lane.
  - **Enabling fix (NA-0622 trigger-persistence gap, surfaced by the Stage-2b vectors):** the main transport send path (`finalize_send_commit`) stored the post-send session state with the trigger-PRESERVING store, so the cleared ratchet-on-reply flag and the N=4/T=15min fallback counters from `qsp_pack` never persisted there: every post-receive send ratcheted forever (the documented D-1239 bounded fallback was dormant, and the approved Stage-2b reseed cadence — a non-boundary send — could never fire on the real path). Fixed: the deliver path now persists `pack.trigger` (exactly as the NA-0622 ack senders already did); the outbox-replay path, which has no pack outcome, still preserves. This makes the D-1239 trigger semantics (ratchet-on-reply + bounded fallback) actually live on the transport path; the `dh_ratchet_e2e_*` assertions are unchanged and still pass.
  - **Design-lock (STOP condition NOT triggered):** a clean, spec-faithful qsc-only wiring exists with the refimpl frozen — the wiring mirrors the NA-0622 DH-trigger pattern; `send_pq_reseed` operates on `Suite2SessionState` and already composes with the DH ratchet on the SEND side; the RECV side needs only the `dh.rk := recv.rk` adoption; the v3 plaintext is length-delimited so `restore_bytes` (exact-length) still receives exactly the frozen QS2S bytes; the ~4 tests that strip the v2 trigger prefix were updated to skip `scka_len + scka` (a non-advertising session has `scka_len == 0`, so the runtime-equivalence comparison is byte-for-byte unchanged).

Bounding: a reseed to a planted key still MIXES into `RK` via `KDF_RK_PQ(RK_old, ss)` with `RK_old` unknown to the attacker, so classical security is unaffected and the PQ layer degrades at worst to "no reseed"; a max-`adv_id` injection is a tracking-DoS for future advertisements. Authenticating the ADV header requires receiver-side trial-open machinery — the same header-auth work area as the deferred NHK reconciliation. (2) The outbox replays only the main message; a crash/drop between the advertisement control push and delivery degrades to the classical status quo until rotation re-advertises.
