Two source lines were added to `/usr/local/sbin/qsl-backup` (`/srv/qbuild/operator`, and `/home/victor/work/qsl/codex` superseding the single-file `QSL_BACKUP_PLAN.md` entry) under the bounded STOP-6 amendment; new script sha256 `4230eccd6d9aa68179fb8595acee570498b79104239b1883fae6c1cd76f071c1`. **RULED: exclude nothing** — *"48 MB is nothing, and an exclusion rule is a thing someone must maintain and get right forever."* Verified in a post-install checkpoint: `operator/` **PRESENT, 807 files**, audit report recoverable, 10/10 `codex/` top-level files, `diff -r --brief` showing only files written after the snapshot began, **0 deletions** on a second run. **⚠ THE CIRCULARITY IS NAMED AND CLOSED: the document describing the backup procedure was not covered by the backup it describes** — `QSL_BACKUP_DIRECTOR_PACKET_20260517.md` was verified absent from the latest snapshot *while B0 was being prepared from that very packet*, which is why its correction (504 → 539 lines, sha256 `555fd000…` → `88e7d164…`) had to be **purely additive**: with no snapshot, the pre-edit text existed nowhere but in its recorded sha256. **§3a SECOND:** `check_repo_registration.sh` made five assertions per repo and **the word "commit" appeared in none of them** — assertion 2 read as health and meant presence. It now asserts **three states**: CURRENT (`ok`, 0), STALE (**FAIL**, **1**, naming the repo and **both shas**), UNREACHABLE (*"could not verify"*, **2**), because *"a check that fails on a network blip trains people to ignore it — a gate that cannot pass teaches bypass."* **EXIT PRECEDENCE IS NORMATIVE AND IMPLEMENTED AS SUCH: exit 1 is evaluated before exit 2, so one repo's network failure can never mask another's real staleness.** Hang-proofed with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `timeout 20`, **proved** rather than asserted: unguarded, `git ls-remote` against a socket that accepts and never replies was still hanging at 45 s; guarded, it was bounded at 20.002 s, and the whole check degraded to UNREACHABLE/exit 2 in 21.6 s. **Scope stated rather than implied: `refs/heads/main` ONLY — PR-ref and tag currency are NOT asserted and are not claimed.** **§3b THIRD, and it is the structurally better half:** `qshell.sh:167` and `qwork.sh:106` both tested that the mirror *directory existed* and treated that as sufficient; both now refresh on **every** worktree creation, so normal use **prevents** staleness rather than merely detecting it, and a mirror can only go stale between lanes rather than across months. The `fitCode` silent-drift seam, the hard half, is untouched. **FILED, NOT FIXED:** **WF-0037** (`new_checkout.sh:63` resolves an explicit `ref` from the mirror before origin is fetched — file-only per §3c, with four ambiguity axes and the reachability limit that `qwork` never passes a `ref`), **WF-0039** (`DOC-OPS-002` enumerates three repos and predates `qsl-desktop`; (2) a workaround that always worked; (3) a documented, correct-to-follow procedure that would have silently regressed three `daily_sources` entries including `/home/victor/.claude`; (4) **a verification instruction that reads as authoritative and is wrong** — the Director's own B0 package shipped four wrong `EXPECT` lines, the worst promising `7a8`/`>` where the truth is `39d38`/`<`, **at the one step whose entire purpose is "anything else ⇒ STOP"**, and a wrong halt condition trains the operator to distrust halt conditions; - **ID:** D-1295
  - **Title:** NA-0669 the three client security fixes of the 2026-07-22 independent audit — recover verification-code entropy (44 → 64 bits) by stripping the constant `QSCFP-` prefix before truncation, fsync the parent directory on the vault write path, and reject rather than lossily transform non-UTF-8 passphrase files; a SHIPPING-CODE lane where both full suites RUN and the green therefore IS evidence
  - **Date:** 2026-07-23
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G3, G4
  - **Decision:** Execute NA-0669 per **QSL-DIR-2026-07-23-605 (D605, APPROVED 2026-07-23, sha256 `4852f471e7bf10d91bd9a8d95d7e08f6af46b8276d816b081e71a74de9274b73`, 374 lines)**, in the directive's order — **C-6 first (unblocked), then C-1a with its lockstep test update, then C-4.** **⚠ THIS LANE IS NOT `docs_only`, AND THAT IS THE POINT:** `scripts/ci/classify_ci_scope.sh` over the implementation PR's file set returns `docs_only=false | workflow_security=false | runtime_critical=true | scope_class=runtime_critical`, so **BOTH FULL SUITES RUN** and a green **could have been red** — verified with a **positive control** (the same classifier still returns `docs_only=true` for a docs-only set), so the classification is itself measured rather than asserted, per NA-0668's standing method. This is the exact inverse of NA-0664/NA-0667/NA-0668, whose spine diffs all classified `docs_only=true` and whose greens proved nothing. **C-6 (`vault/mod.rs` `write_vault_atomic`):** one line, `crate::fsync_dir_best_effort(parent)` after `fs::rename`, byte-parallel to the pre-existing `vault_init_core` call; `sync_all()` persisted the tmp file's CONTENTS but never the DIRECTORY ENTRY the rename creates. Its importance is wider than one write path — the function has **THREE callers** (`secret_set:240`, `secret_set_with_passphrase:273`, `persist_session:385`), i.e. **every steady-state vault mutation in the product** (contacts, ratchet state, timeline, identity secrets after init), and it was the **ONLY** rename-then-nothing site in the crate while the other durability paths all fsync; `parent` was already bound and the helper is best-effort by construction, so it adds no error path. **⚠ THE EVIDENCE BOUNDARY IS STATED RATHER THAN BLURRED: no test in the suite can observe C-6** — directory-entry durability is only visible across a power failure — so **the suite green proves NON-REGRESSION for C-6 and nothing more**; what supports it is the parity argument, not the check. **C-1a (`identity/mod.rs:527`):** the alphanumeric filter dropped the hyphen of `IDENTITY_FP_PREFIX` but KEPT its five letters, so five of sixteen displayed characters were constant and every code ever shown began `QSCF-P`; strip the prefix before the filter, width 16 and `4-4-4-4-checksum` grouping unchanged, non-prefixed input left alone (the function is `pub` and reachable from qsl-desktop). **MEASURED THROUGH THE REAL PRODUCTION FUNCTION, NOT A MODEL** — five real identities from the real built binary, plus 4000 real-shaped fingerprints through the `qsc` library linked as an external consumer crate, built once from the base tree and once from the fixed tree: constant display positions go `[0,1,2,3,4,5,9,14,19]` → `"QSCF-P---"` to `[4,9,14,19]` → `"----"`, and varying hex `11 → 16`, i.e. **44 → 64 bits**, position-for-position identical to the directive's modeled table. **⚠ 64 BITS AT WIDTH 16, NOT THE INTENT'S 88/22** — 16 hex chars is 64 bits, 88 needs 22, which needs the target-width change this lane excludes and is not divisible by the four-character grouping; corrected in the directive before execution. **⚠ ONE ARITHMETIC CORRECTION TO THE DIRECTIVE ITSELF, RECORDED NOT QUIETLY FIXED:** §1a calls the result "a 20-fold reduction in collision probability" when it is a **20-BIT** reduction, a factor of **2²⁰ ≈ 1,048,576**; the bit figures and every ruling resting on them are correct and unaffected. **⚠ THE SHADOW COPY (`tests/identity_binding.rs:37`) WAS UPDATED IN LOCKSTEP AND DELIBERATELY KEPT AS A DUPLICATE** rather than replaced by an import — its separateness is precisely what makes the test a real check that the CLI and the formula agree instead of a tautology. **No assertion was weakened and no expected value needed editing, for a stronger reason than the directive anticipated: the test COMPUTES its expected code rather than pinning a literal, so the lockstep formula update IS the value update.** **A THIRD CALL SITE THE DIRECTIVE DID NOT NAME was found by sweeping all callers rather than working from its list** — `tests/NA_0649_gui_surface.rs:311-312` — and is unaffected, asserting only shape and determinism; `identity_ux.rs:141-142` and `NA_0634:89-95` were likewise confirmed unaffected rather than assumed. **C-4 (`vault/mod.rs` `read_passphrase_file`): RULED REJECT, NOT RAW BYTES.** `from_utf8_lossy` collapsed invalid bytes to U+FFFD; measured by enumerating the COMPLETE single-byte input space through Rust's real function, one random byte retains **129 distinct outcomes and Shannon H = 4.500 bits of 8** (43.8% destroyed — all 128 bytes `0x80-0xFF` collapse to one character), so `head -c 32 /dev/urandom > pass.txt` produced a vault the operator believed held 256 bits and which held **≈144**, confirming the audit's 145–160; corroborated over 200,000 random 32-byte trials in which **ZERO were valid UTF-8** (mean 13.35 replacements per file). Raw-bytes-end-to-end is the better design and was rejected as **uncontained** — ~10 sites across two files including **two `pub` signature changes on the surface qsl-desktop links against** — and belongs with the vault-format lane. Reject is one line, the existing error code, no signature change, and converts a **silent degradation into a loud, diagnosable failure at the moment of use**, while removing the two-ingress asymmetry that was the tell (stdin already errored via `read_to_string`). **OBSERVED WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL:** the base binary **silently accepted** the raw file (exit 0) and the fixed binary **rejects** it (`vault_passphrase_file_read_failed`, exit 1), so the rejection is a measured behavior change rather than a broken rig; base64 of the SAME 32 bytes round-trips init → rotate → show with **all 256 bits reaching Argon2id byte-for-byte** (the pre-fix path handed Argon2id **64 bytes** for a 32-byte file — a longer string carrying less information). **BOTH MIGRATION BREAKS WERE RULED ACCEPTED WITH NO MIGRATION, KNOWINGLY RATHER THAN BY DISCOVERY.** (1) **F1(a): `identity_pin_matches_seen:562` IS NOT TOUCHED** — verification codes ARE stored as pins today (`contacts/mod.rs:908`/`:918` store `--fp` verbatim; the `(None,None)` arm at `:886` performs no key check at all), the behavior is covered by the named test `handshake_accepts_verification_code_pin_without_peer_mismatch`, and deleting the branch is a **product decision** rather than a one-line security fix; C-1a alone takes that comparison 44 → 64 bits, which is the win available without one. **(b) was declined explicitly** — one new marker is not worth a vocabulary change in a lane scoped to three fixes. **Recorded because it cuts the other way:** `src/adversarial/binding_fuzz.rs:396 trusted_pin_matches_seen` is a strict full-fingerprint compare with **no code branch**, and the production result is computed into `_canonical_pin_matches` and **DISCARDED** in its favour (`handshake/mod.rs:990`/`:1046`/`:1093`), so the strict semantics are already the modeled and attested ones and the production leniency is a **known, unasserted divergence from the model**; the oracle was NOT edited (a STOP condition). **⚠ C-1a BREAKS EVERY EXISTING CODE-PINNED CONTACT REGARDLESS OF F1** — the on-disk old-format string can never equal the newly-recomputed code, so every subsequent handshake yields `peer_mismatch`; this follows from changing the FORMAT, not the matcher. (2) **F2: every existing vault created from a non-UTF-8 passphrase file becomes PERMANENTLY UNOPENABLE** — the lossy transform ran at BOTH init and unlock, so such vaults were self-consistent, and either candidate fix breaks that; **demonstrated live rather than asserted**, and reject is the kinder candidate because it fails with the named error rather than as an indistinguishable wrong key, hitting precisely the `/dev/urandom` operator who was trying hardest. **RULED NOT TRIVIAL, REPORTED NOT FIXED:** the trailing-newline stripper is a `while` loop running at both init and unlock, so changing it silently changes the derived key for anyone whose file ended in more than one newline, and `read_passphrase_from_stdin` carries the identical loop — any fix must move both together. **PHASE 0 RE-ANCHORED EVERY file:line AT THE SEATING BASE rather than trusting the directive:** anchors were exact at `14a2464c` and the seat was `62118874`, and `git diff --name-status` between them returns **`M NEXT_ACTIONS.md` and nothing else**, with each anchor then confirmed individually — no drift, so nothing was edited at a shifted line. **SCOPE DISCIPLINE WAS THE LANE'S SECOND DELIVERABLE:** three files touched, all in §5a; the functional change is **three lines**; `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` verified untouched **including after building an external consumer crate against the tree** (the one step that could plausibly have moved them); `binding_fuzz.rs` and `:562` byte-unchanged; **and NOTHING NEW WAS FILED in `IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md`** — observations went to the operator relay, not the ledger. **rustfmt:** the crate carries pre-existing drift across 42 files (the known owed micro-lane); verified by diffing the complete `cargo fmt --check` output before and after that this lane introduces **ZERO new drift** and repairs none. **CROSS-REPO, REPORT ONLY:** C-1a changes the code qsl-desktop displays, **but only when desktop bumps its qsc pin**, a separate deliberate lane; two desktop artifacts go stale at that moment (`docs/DESIGN_SPEC_AppendixD.md:100`/`:221`, `ui/style.css:280`), **no desktop test pins the format so desktop CI will not break**, and no spine doc pins it either. **C-2 (constant-time bearer compare) is a separate `qsl-server` lane and is not touched here.** Successor: the **vault-format lane**, which now owns C-1b, the target-width decision, the `identity_pin_matches_seen` product ruling, the C-4 raw-bytes form and the newline stripper — a coherent set worth sizing sooner than planned.
  - **Rationale:** The three defects are real, present, and correctly located, and each is a one-line fix whose cost is far below its benefit: 20 bits of verification-code strength at zero UX cost, durability for every steady-state vault mutation in a no-recovery product, and the conversion of a silent 112-bit entropy loss into a diagnosable error. Taking them together in one small lane keeps the change surface auditable (three lines of behavior across three files) while the two product-shaped questions they touch — the code-as-pin semantics and the raw-bytes passphrase pipeline — are deliberately deferred to the vault-format lane that already owns their siblings, rather than being smuggled into a lane scoped to one-line fixes. The lane is also the first in five to ship code, which makes its CI green load-bearing for the first time in that run and discharges NA-0668's standing method by construction.
  - **Security invariants introduced/changed:**
    - Verification-code machine comparison strength rises from **44 to 64 bits** for any contact pinned by code; the human-comparable code no longer leaks six constant leading characters.
    - Every steady-state vault mutation (`secret_set`, `secret_set_with_passphrase`, `persist_session`) now fsyncs the parent directory after the atomic rename, closing the last rename-then-nothing site in the crate.
    - A non-UTF-8 passphrase file is now **rejected** rather than silently transformed; passphrase entropy reaching Argon2id is byte-exact with the file, and file and stdin ingress now behave identically.
    - **Two accepted breaking changes, no migration (pre-release):** existing code-pinned contacts yield `peer_mismatch`; existing vaults created from non-UTF-8 passphrase files become permanently unopenable.
    - No protocol, wire, relay, handshake, ratchet, or cryptographic-primitive semantics change. No marker-vocabulary change. No new error code. No `pub` signature change. No new dependency.
  - **Alternatives considered:**
    - **F1(b)** — emit a marker when the code branch produced a pin match, making the 64-bit comparison observable. **Declined explicitly:** it adds one marker to the vocabulary, and past lanes track "no marker-vocabulary change" as a property.
    - **F1(c)** — delete or gate the code-accepting branch now. **Declined:** it is a product change that breaks a documented, named-test workflow, and it rides the vault-format lane with C-1b and the width decision.
    - **C-4 raw bytes end-to-end** — the better design; **declined as uncontained** (~10 sites, two `pub` signature changes on the qsl-desktop-facing surface). Deferred to the vault-format lane.
    - **Widening the code to 20 or 24 characters** to reach 88 bits — **explicitly out of scope**; assigned to the vault-format lane, and not divisible by the display grouping at 22.
    - **Replacing the `identity_binding.rs` shadow copy with an import** — **rejected**: it would turn a real cross-check into a tautology.
  - **Implications for spec/impl/tests:**
    - `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/identity/mod.rs`, `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/vault/mod.rs`, `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/tests/identity_binding.rs`, and — **added by operator ruling (A)** — `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/tests/identity_foundation_contract_na0217d.rs`: the **four** files touched.
    - **⚠ THERE WERE THREE COPIES OF THE FORMATTER, NOT TWO, AND THE SUITE CAUGHT THE THIRD.** The first full `cargo test -p qsc` went RED on `verification_code_pin_preserves_handshake_contract` (`na0217d.rs`), which pins a code via a **second byte-identical shadow copy** (`na0217d.rs:133`, named `verification_code_from_fingerprint` — no `format_` prefix, which is why symbol-name sweeps missed it). Under ruling (A) it was given the identical lockstep prefix-strip, duplicate kept, assertion at `:294` unchanged. **Both** `tests/identity_binding.rs:37` **and** `tests/identity_foundation_contract_na0217d.rs:133` must now be kept in lockstep with the production formatter forever, and both must remain duplicates rather than imports.
    - **Root-cause finding (generalizable, recorded not filed):** hunt duplicate implementations by sweeping for a distinctive **body fragment/constant** (here the Crockford alphabet), not the symbol name — names diverge, bodies do not. Same class as the NA-0668 costume set: an instrument pointed slightly off the question. The suite demonstrating it could reject a real defect is the lane's strongest evidence item — stronger than a first-try green.
    - **No fourth copy.** qsl-desktop (mirror main `02cc9b9`, body-swept) holds none of its own — it calls the qsc production symbol (`commands.rs:82`, `slice_a_flows.rs:50`) and pins no format literal, so desktop CI will not break on the pin bump. Its displayed verification code changes when it next bumps its qsc pin; two of its artifacts go stale at that moment (`DESIGN_SPEC_AppendixD.md:100`/`:221`, `ui/style.css:280`). Report-only in this lane.
    - The vault-format lane inherits C-1b, the target-width decision, the `identity_pin_matches_seen` ruling, the C-4 raw-bytes form, and the newline stripper.

- **ID:** D-1296
  - **Title:** NA-0669 closeout — the three 2026-07-22 audit client security fixes shipped and merged (D-1295 as `ccc6c008`); this lane's green is EVIDENCE, not the empty green of the four docs-only lanes before it, because the suite was demonstrated to REJECT a real defect (shadow #2, the third copy of the verification-code formatter) before it was trusted to accept
  - **Date:** 2026-07-23
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G3, G4
  - **Decision:** Close NA-0669 per **QSL-DIR-2026-07-23-605 (D605)** and operator ruling (A). The implementation (D-1295) merged as `ccc6c008` over head `3d32a1c0`; the queue returns to `READY=NONE | HIGHEST_NA=0669 | HIGHEST_D=1296`. **THE THREE SHIPPED FIXES, IN PLAIN TERMS FOR THE RECORD:** **C-1a** takes the verification code from **44 to 64 bits** by stripping the constant `QSCFP-` prefix before truncating — the alphanumeric filter had dropped the prefix's hyphen but kept its five letters, so five of sixteen displayed characters were constant and every code ever shown began `QSCF-P`. **C-6** adds the **parent-directory fsync that `vault_init_core` already had** to `write_vault_atomic` after its rename, closing a crash window in which a power loss could lose the **directory entry** — and thus the whole store — while the tmp file's contents were durable; the site has three callers (`secret_set`, `secret_set_with_passphrase`, `persist_session`), i.e. every steady-state vault mutation, and was the crate's only rename-then-nothing site. **C-4** **rejects non-UTF-8 passphrase files** (`String::from_utf8`) instead of running them through `from_utf8_lossy`, which silently discarded ~44% of their entropy (measured Shannon H = 4.500 bits of 8 per random byte; all 128 bytes `0x80-0xFF` collapse to U+FFFD), so `head -c 32 /dev/urandom > pass.txt` yielded a ~144-bit vault the operator believed was 256-bit. **⚠ THIS LANE'S GREEN IS EVIDENCE, AND THE CONTRAST IS THE POINT.** The four lanes immediately preceding — NA-0664, NA-0666, NA-0667, NA-0668 — all shipped `docs_only=true` diffs, so `classify_ci_scope.sh` skipped both full suites and their green checks carried no information about the work (NA-0668's real validation had to come from watching a tooling check fail on purpose, because no CI could see the tooling). **This lane changed `src/`, classified `runtime_critical`, so both full suites AND the formal proofs RAN rather than skipped** — 34 checks green on PR #1630, the only 2 skips being the known NA-0633 PR-skips of `qsc-linux-full-suite`/`macos-qsc-full-serial` (for which the local `cargo test -p qsc` green is the compensating evidence). **And the instrument was demonstrated to reject a real defect before it was trusted to accept:** the first full local run went **RED** on `verification_code_pin_preserves_handshake_contract`, which pinned a code via a **third copy of the formatter the census missed** — shadow #2, `verification_code_from_fingerprint` at `tests/identity_foundation_contract_na0217d.rs:133`. It was fixed under **operator ruling (A)**, which extended §5a to that one file for the identical lockstep prefix-strip (duplicate kept, assertion at `:294` unchanged — "update the derivation," not "weaken an assertion"), and the re-run completed clean: **434 passed, 0 failed, `CARGO_EXIT=0`.** A first-try green would have been a weaker evidence story; NA-0668's standing method (*a negative result is only evidence if the instrument could have returned positive*) is discharged here by observation, not argument. **ROOT-CAUSE FINDING, recorded not filed:** shadow #2 is named without the `format_` prefix, so every sweep keyed on the symbol name missed it — the directive's authoring grep and the executor's Phase-0 caller-sweep both; only a sweep for the **function body** (the Crockford constant `0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ`) finds all three copies. **Lesson: hunt duplicate implementations by a distinctive body fragment, not the symbol name — names diverge, bodies do not** — the same class as NA-0668's costume set, an instrument pointed slightly off the question. **NO FOURTH COPY:** qsl-desktop (mirror main `02cc9b9`, body-swept) holds none of its own, calls the qsc production symbol (`commands.rs:82`, `slice_a_flows.rs:50`) and pins no format literal, so its CI will not break on the pin bump; the §5b staleness (`DESIGN_SPEC_AppendixD.md`, `ui/style.css`) lands only when desktop next bumps its qsc pin. **⚠ CORRECTION OF THE D-1295 CHARACTERIZATION:** D-1295 called the successor "the vault-format lane" and said it "owns" the deferred items. Per operator §9.7 that is imprecise — **the four owed items ride the vault WORK, and NONE of them is a vault-FORMAT change:** (1) the **C-1 verification-code target-width decision** (20/24, to reach beyond 64 bits), (2) the **C-1b checksum transposition weakness**, (3) **C-4's raw-bytes form** (the uncontained ~10-site passphrase-pipeline change deferred here), and (4) the **trailing-newline stripper** (a `while` loop self-consistent at init and unlock, so any fix must move both together). Separately, **`identity_pin_matches_seen:562` stays untouched per F1(a)** and is to be ruled together with the width decision. **C-2** (constant-time bearer compare) remains a separate `qsl-server` lane. **Nothing new was filed in `IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md`** — observations went to the operator relay; scope discipline (four files, three lines of behavior plus two lockstep test updates) was the lane's second deliverable. Queue returns to `READY=NONE`; the operator promotes; the executor cannot self-promote.
  - **Rationale:** The three fixes are shipped, merged, and validated by a suite that was proven capable of failing on this exact change set — the strongest form of the evidence the lane was defined to produce, and the structural inverse of the four docs-only greens that preceded it. The closeout records the shipped fixes in plain terms, states the green-as-evidence contrast explicitly, corrects the D-1295 "vault-format" phrasing to "vault work / not a format change" per the operator, and carries the four deferred items plus the `:562` ruling forward without filing new ledger entries, preserving the scope discipline the lane was also meant to demonstrate.
  - **Security invariants introduced/changed:** None beyond those recorded in D-1295 (verification-code machine comparison 44→64 bits for code-pinned contacts; parent-directory fsync on every steady-state vault mutation; non-UTF-8 passphrase files rejected rather than lossily transformed; two accepted pre-release migration breaks with no migration). No protocol, wire, handshake, ratchet, or cryptographic-primitive change; no marker-vocabulary change; no new error code; no new dependency. This closeout ships governance records only.
  - **Alternatives considered:**
    - **Filing the three fixes as new `IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md` entries.** Declined — the ledger tracks no audit findings and the lane's scope discipline was to file nothing new; the plain-terms record lives in this decision, the journal and TRACEABILITY instead.
    - **Carrying the D-1295 "vault-format lane" phrasing forward unchanged.** Declined per operator §9.7 — none of the four owed items is a vault-format change, and mislabeling them would misdirect the successor's scoping.
  - **Implications for spec/impl/tests:**
    - Queue at `READY=NONE | HIGHEST_NA=0669 | HIGHEST_D=1296`; helper `READY_COUNT 0` with exit 2 is CORRECT at `READY=NONE` (`--allow-nonready-count` not passed) and is not a failure.
    - The successor **vault work** inherits four items (target-width decision, C-1b checksum transposition, C-4 raw-bytes form, newline stripper), **none a vault-format change**, plus the `identity_pin_matches_seen:562` ruling to be decided with the width decision.
    - Both formatter test shadow copies (`identity_binding.rs:37`, `identity_foundation_contract_na0217d.rs:133`) must be kept in lockstep with the production formatter forever and must remain duplicates rather than imports.
    - qsl-desktop's displayed verification code changes when it next bumps its qsc pin; `DESIGN_SPEC_AppendixD.md` and `ui/style.css` go stale at that moment. Desktop pin-bump lane's concern.
  - **References:** NA-0669; D605 (`QSL-DIR-2026-07-23-605`, approved 2026-07-23, sha256 `4852f471e7bf10d91bd9a8d95d7e08f6af46b8276d816b081e71a74de9274b73`, 374 lines); operator ruling (A) extending §5a to `tests/identity_foundation_contract_na0217d.rs` for the one lockstep edit; D-1295 (the implementation decision this closes, merged as `ccc6c008` over head `3d32a1c0`, PR #1630); D-1294 (NA-0668, whose standing method this lane discharges by observation); the 2026-07-22 independent audit (findings C-1a, C-4, C-6; C-1b, C-2 and the target-width decision deliberately out of scope); `docs/governance/evidence/NA-0669_as_built.md`; `tests/NA-0669_audit_client_security_fixes_testplan.md`; `docs/ops/ROLLING_OPERATIONS_JOURNAL.md` (2026-07-23 entry + closeout). **Nothing was filed in `docs/ops/IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md` — deliberately.**

- **ID:** D-1297
  - **Title:** NA-0670 closeout — the last unfixed HIGH of the 2026-07-22 independent audit (C-2) shipped: qsl-server `auth_ok` now compares the bearer token in constant time (SHA-256 both sides, then the client's `hs_ct_eq_32` XOR-fold), closing a remote timing oracle on the one network-exposed component; like NA-0669 and unlike the four docs-only lanes before it, the qsl-server implementation PR changed `src/` so its required `rust` check RAN and its green IS evidence for the behavioural half
  - **Date:** 2026-07-23
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G4
  - **Decision:** Close NA-0670 per **QSL-DIR-2026-07-23-606 (D606)**. The qsl-server implementation (satellite decision **D-0014**) merged as `5235c2bf` (PR #64) over base `b4f86a3c`; the queue returns to `READY=NONE | HIGHEST_NA=0670 | HIGHEST_D=1297`. **THE FIX, IN PLAIN TERMS:** `auth_ok`'s final `provided == token` used `str::eq`, which short-circuits on the first differing byte — a **remote timing oracle** on the one component deliberately exposed to the network, in the low-jitter LAN/tailnet regime where byte-at-a-time statistical amplification is actually practical. It is now `ct_eq_secret(provided, token)`, a private helper that reduces both sides to a fixed 32-byte SHA-256 digest and folds them with an XOR-accumulate loop over all 32 bytes (`diff |= da[i] ^ db[i]`, then `diff == 0`) — the exact shape of the qsc client's `hs_ct_eq_32` (ENG-0003) and consistent with this file's own `route_key_for`, which already hashes the **other** secret (the route token), so the relay now treats both its secrets the same way (the strongest form of the fix, §1b). Hashing normalises both inputs to 32 bytes, so the fold does identical work for every input, **closing the length leak** the audit offered as optional (§2c). The two `return false` guards (missing / malformed `Authorization`) are kept — they branch on attacker-known request shape, not on the secret. **NO dependency change:** `sha2` is already a direct dependency and `use sha2::{Digest, Sha256}` already imported; `subtle` was **deliberately NOT added** (it is present in `Cargo.lock` only via rustls under the reqwest DEV-dependency; a direct use would newly enter the production graph, and — being defined for equal-length slices — would not close the length leak without a length-visible branch; §2b/§2c) — the `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` diff is verified empty. **NO wire/API/protocol/schema/env change;** the four gated handlers (`server-info`, `push`, `pull`, `pull/ack`) still reject-before-mutation because `auth_ok` remains their first statement. **⚠ THIS LANE'S GREEN IS EVIDENCE, AND THE DISTINCTION IS STATED SO THE CLOSEOUT DOES NOT INHERIT THE WRONG CAVEAT:** the qsl-server implementation PR changed `src/lib.rs`, so `classify_ci_scope` returns runtime/non-docs and the required `rust` check **RAN** — green on `82df531`, the **exact reviewed commit** (run head == PR head == local HEAD, 1m36s). That green is real evidence for the **behavioural** half (auth still accepts the right token and rejects wrong ones, including the same-length case, under CI). It is the inverse of the queue-promotion PR (docs_only, green proved nothing) and of the four docs-only lanes NA-0664/0666/0667/0668. **The constant-time property ITSELF is STRUCTURAL — fixed work over the full 32-byte digest, no data-dependent early return — verified by READING, not by measurement; no timing proof was run or claimed (§3.4 held).** A **same-length wrong-token test** was added (`"topsecreX"` vs `"topsecret"`, both 9 bytes): the pre-existing wrong-token test uses different-length tokens, so `==` rejected on length before comparing a single byte and **passed against the buggy code** — the same-length case is the only behavioural test that exercises the fold, and it proves the fold's ANSWER (reject + no mutation), not its timing. Phase 0 re-verified every §0/§1 anchor at the seating base `b4f86a3c` (`provided == token` at `src/lib.rs:507` exactly; `sha2` imported at `:10`; `route_key_for` at `:486`; the `==` body-sweep confirming `:507` is the **sole** secret comparison — so no second fix is owed, §1c). **FOUR LEDGER FILINGS, NONE FIXED (scope discipline held — one function, nothing else touched):** ENG-0063 (precompute `Sha256::digest(token)` once at `AppState` construction — a refinement riding the `new_with_auth*` constructor chain, §5), ENG-0064 (the two-repo seat leaked qsl-protocol's `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` into the qsl-server seat, defeating the per-repo cache separation NA-0667's registration established — worked around with an explicit pin, not fixed), ENG-0065 (a pre-existing flaky log-capture test, `tests::logs_do_not_contain_raw_channel`, **surfaced not caused** by the required new test at 6-core contention — CI-irrelevant at ≤4 threads), ENG-0066 (qsl-server `TRACEABILITY.md` lapsed for three satellite lanes). Commit identity on the qsl-server implementation commit and on this closeout is the GH007 noreply (`238594419+Tebbens4832@users.noreply.github.com`), author and committer, trailers empty, verified on the object (WF-0029 per-commit override). Queue returns to `READY=NONE`; the operator promotes; the executor cannot self-promote.
  - **Rationale:** The last unfixed HIGH of the independent audit is shipped on the single network-exposed component, in the file's own existing idiom (SHA-256 then fold), with no dependency, wire, or behavioural change. Because the implementation PR changed `src/`, its required `rust` check ran and its green is real evidence for the behavioural half — while the constant-time property remains a structural, read-verified claim, never a measured one, holding the near-miss line before there is a near-miss. Unlike NA-0669, this lane DID file — four ledger entries — because each records a real, decision-bearing finding that would otherwise evaporate in a relay (an observation that lives only in a turn record never gets scheduled), and filing them is recording, not a second fix; scope discipline barred doing any of that work inside a one-function lane, and none was done.
  - **Security invariants introduced/changed:** The relay's bearer-token comparison is now **constant-time** (fixed work over a 32-byte digest, no data-dependent early return) and **length-independent**, removing a remote timing oracle on the network-exposed shared secret. `auth_ok` accepts and rejects EXACTLY the tokens it did before. No protocol, wire, handshake, ratchet, vault, or cryptographic-primitive change; no marker-vocabulary change; no new error code; no new dependency. A residual **constant per-deployment** timing offset from re-hashing the token on each request remains (proportional to the token's block count, not per-guess and not content-revealing); it is filed as ENG-0063, not folded in. This closeout ships governance records only.
  - **Alternatives considered:**
    - **`subtle::ConstantTimeEq` on the raw bytes.** Declined (§2b/§2c) — it would newly enter the production dependency graph, and being defined for equal-length slices it would not close the length leak without a length-visible branch; hashing-first closes it for free and yields the `hs_ct_eq_32` idiom the file already uses.
    - **HMAC with a random per-process key.** Declined (§2d) — its random key defends against precomputation, but an attacker who already holds a candidate token can simply send it; plain SHA-256 delivers the property actually needed (comparison time independent of matching-prefix length) with no added machinery.
    - **Precomputing the token digest at `AppState` construction.** Deferred and filed as ENG-0063 — it removes the secret from the per-request path and erases the block-count offset, but touches the multi-constructor `new_with_auth*` chain, correctly out of a one-function lane.
    - **Filing nothing (the NA-0669 posture).** Declined — the four findings are real and decision-bearing; recording them at closeout is the correct home and does not reopen scope discipline.
  - **Implications for spec/impl/tests:**
    - Queue at `READY=NONE | HIGHEST_NA=0670 | HIGHEST_D=1297`; helper `READY_COUNT 0` with exit 2 is CORRECT at `READY=NONE` (`--allow-nonready-count` not passed) and is not a failure.
    - qsl-server records satellite decision **D-0014** and a `TRACEABILITY.md` row; the required `rust` check ran green on the implementation PR (#64, head `82df531`, merged `5235c2bf`).
    - No qsl-desktop, qsc, or protocol/spec change. The 2026-07-22 audit finding **C-2 is now closed**, and with it the last audit HIGH; the route-token path (`route_key_for`) is named as evidence, not a target, and is byte-unchanged.
    - Four new `IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md` entries (ENG-0063…ENG-0066), all `open`, none fixed by this lane.
  - **References:** NA-0670; D606 (`QSL-DIR-2026-07-23-606`, approved 2026-07-23, sha256 `ef3bd063f936564935b86e806e459e2bc93be6a4b52fdba685611e43e8a177ca`, 284 lines); D-0014 (qsl-server satellite decision, merged as `5235c2bf`, PR #64 over base `b4f86a3c`); the 2026-07-22 independent audit finding **C-2** (the last unfixed HIGH, and the only one outside the spine); qsl-protocol **ENG-0003** (client `hs_ct_eq_32`); this closeout's four filings **ENG-0063 / ENG-0064 / ENG-0065 / ENG-0066**; `docs/governance/evidence/NA-0670_as_built.md`; `tests/NA-0670_qsl_server_c2_constant_time_bearer_testplan.md`; `docs/ops/ROLLING_OPERATIONS_JOURNAL.md` (2026-07-23 NA-0670 closeout entry).

- **ID:** D-1298
  - **Title:** NA-0671 measurement — the Argon2id (vault-KDF) derivations per relay operation, MEASURED in-process against two real relays: SEND = **20**, PULL = **15**, ACK = **18** on an open relay (RELEASE, passphrase vault) — the 2026-07-22 audit's inferred 7–9/send was a **~2.5× undercount**, so per-send Argon2id is ~388 ms (not ~135–175 ms); this lane FIXES NOTHING, and because the measurement harness is `#[ignore]` and the qsc full suite skips on PRs, **a green is NOT the evidence — the captured numbers are**
  - **Date:** 2026-07-23
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G4
  - **Decision:** Per **QSL-DIR-2026-07-23-607 (D607)**, replace the 2026-07-22 audit's *inference* (7–9 derivations/relay-op from static path-reading) with an *instrument*. A new `#[ignore]` harness (`qsl/qsl-client/qsc/tests/NA_0671_vault_kdf_cost.rs`) stands up two real in-process `qsl-server` relays (open and token-auth), drives a full authenticated pair to steady state via subprocess CLI (setup is NOT measured), then brackets the **in-process** library calls `transport::send_execute` / `transport::receive_execute` with `vault::perf_snapshot()` + `std::time::Instant`. **MEASURED, RELEASE, `key_source==1` (passphrase) vault, unlocked** — per operation, cold and warm, not aggregated: **SEND 20, PULL 15, ACK(lease) 18** derivations on an **open** relay; **SEND 19, PULL 14, ACK 16** on a **token-auth** (vault-stored bearer) relay; **SEND 18** with the bearer supplied via `QSC_RELAY_TOKEN` **env** (which short-circuits the token+token-file vault probes). At the shipped 19.4 ms/derivation that is **SEND ≈ 388 ms, PULL ≈ 291 ms, ACK ≈ 349 ms**; at the OWASP-minimum 41.1 ms (a **multiply-by constant** — no KDF parameter was changed) **SEND ≈ 822 ms**. The audit's 7–9/send was a **~2.5× undercount**; the real cost sits **above** the 90–180 ms band the NA-0664 handoff said "would restore urgency." **THE COUNTER HAZARD, NAMED (OBS-3):** `PERF_KDF_CALLS.fetch_add(1)` is at the TOP of `derive_runtime_key`, before the `match key_source`, so it counts **vault opens, not Argon2id hashes** — equal to the hash count only on an unlocked passphrase vault; a future keychain-side measurement must not reuse these as Argon2 cost. Validity was established before any op number was trusted: a **positive control** (one lone `secret_get` on a present key) returned exactly **1** derivation at ~19.4 ms (the instrument returns positive), and every op's count was **cross-checked against wall-clock** (`wall_ms/19.4` tracks the count within ~3–6%, so every counted derivation was a real ~19 ms Argon2id — no sub-millisecond no-op "KDF calls" to exclude; **the timing governs and did not disagree**). **AMORTISATION: NONE** — cold == warm for every op, and two consecutive `secret_get`s each cost 1 derivation, confirming nothing caches the derived key within a process (so a long-lived GUI/daemon would amortise nothing, and the CLI's cold-per-command cost IS the full count). **ABSENT-SECRET-PROBE SUB-RESULT (OBS-2), promoted to a first-class number:** on an open relay SEND pays **3 absent probes** — `secret_get` for the relay token, token-file, and CA-file, all returning `None` yet each paying a full ~19.4 ms (≈58 ms, ≈15% of the send) — confirmed empirically by the auth-mode deltas (open 20 → token-env 18 removes both token+token-file probes; open → token-vault 19 short-circuits token-file). "Don't probe for what isn't there" is therefore a **distinct, cheaper remedy class** than the vault-format work (removes ~3 derivations/op, zero format change) — but a **partial** (SEND 20 → 17): the cost is dominated by the **present**-secret re-derivations (contacts/session/timeline re-loaded, uncached, by each gate), which only key-caching removes. **NEAR-MISS DISPOSITION:** the armed hypothesis was 7–9/SEND; the measured 20 REFUTES it, and the second look was taken regardless — a fresh process reproduced every count identically, the auth-mode deltas match the token/token-file short-circuit mechanism exactly, and the wall-clock cross-check rules out counter inflation. **This lane ships no remedy;** the number is the sizing input for the subsequent vault-decision lane, recorded (not started) here.
  - **Rationale:** The entire vault decision (envelope encryption vs session-key caching vs raising Argon2id to the OWASP minimum) was being sized against an inference that proved 2.5× low. A re-runnable instrument, validated by a positive control and a wall-clock cross-check and confirmed across a fresh process and two auth modes, replaces it with a defensible number and — as a bonus first-class sub-result — surfaces a cheaper, localized remedy class (absent-secret-probe elimination) that the aggregate total would have hidden. The measurement is in-process because `perf_snapshot`'s counters are process-global atomics that die with a subprocess CLI child; the operation is a real library call, so the number is the shipped cold-per-command cost, not a reconstruction.
  - **Security invariants introduced/changed:** None. No `src/` runtime change; `secret_get`/`secret_set`/`load_vault_runtime`/`derive_runtime_key`, the `PERF_*` counters and their increment sites, `PROCESS_PASSPHRASE`, and `KDF_M_KIB`/`KDF_T`/`KDF_P` are untouched. No dependency change (`Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` diff empty). No caching / session-key cache / envelope encryption / KDF-parameter change was added — those are explicitly the next lane's input. The only additions are one `#[ignore]` test harness and one evidence artifact.
  - **Alternatives considered:**
    - **Reuse an existing e2e scaffold (F2 default).** Not possible — every full-relay-op e2e drives the CLI as subprocesses whose counters are unreadable from the parent, and the one in-process passphrase-vault scaffold (`NA_0649_gui_surface.rs`) never touches a relay operation. Built a standalone in-process send/pull/ack driver (~370-line file) reusing only `common`'s real-relay + vault-init helpers — the "standalone, none fit" class, settling the F2 ~30-vs-~100–150-line estimate against reality.
    - **Measure token mode by client-side toggle against one open relay.** Declined for ambiguity — used two real relays (open + token) so every measured send/pull/ack is a genuinely successful operation in its own auth mode.
    - **Trust the static site-count for the mechanism breakdown.** Declined as the whole premise — static reading is what produced the 2.5×-low 7–9. The total (20/15/18) and the auth=3 / timeline=2 slices are measured; only the per-site attribution is from the code map, and is labeled as such.
    - **File an ENG for the counter-naming hazard (OBS-3).** Declined per directive — it lives in the evidence artifact that qualifies it, so a future reader meets it in context; a detached ledger entry would strand it.
  - **Implications for spec/impl/tests:**
    - The subsequent vault-decision lane sizes against **SEND 20 / PULL 15 / ACK 18** (open; 19/14/16 token), i.e. ~388/291/349 ms release and ~822/616/740 ms at the OWASP minimum — not 7–9/send. Three remedy classes are now sized: (a) session-key cache / envelope encryption (removes the per-`secret_get` re-derivation, addresses the whole cost); (b) request-scoped de-duplication of the redundant contacts/session loads (collapses ~20 to a handful, no format change); (c) absent-secret-probe elimination (~3/op, ~58 ms/send, cheapest but partial). Auth mode barely moves the total, so (c) alone is insufficient — the defect is no key caching.

This closeout records the number as the **subsequent vault-decision lane's input, in the terms the operator required — and it ships no remedy.** **⚠ THE MEASUREMENT REFUTES THE FRAME, NOT JUST THE FIGURE.** The 2026-07-22 audit inferred 7–9 Argon2id derivations/send (~135–175 ms) and framed the vault decision as "restore urgency IF inside 90–180 ms." Fixed in two touch points — creation (`new_checkout.sh`) and reuse (`qwork.sh`), because fixing only creation would have left most existing seats wrong — and **proved with a POSITIVE CONTROL** (the instrument was made to return positive first). Result class **SEAT_IDENTITY_FIX_PASS**. **PHASE 2 (qsl-desktop #10, D-0010, merge `a836eaf`, `[rust]` green, 70/0/1):** the `[F.1-COMMIT]` REVERSAL — one unified Save commits everything through the EXISTING trios; **Test SAVES FIRST** then probes the just-saved state; the four per-field Set/Clear buttons REMOVED for per-field *"remove it"* links whose removal is PENDING until the next commit and is cancelled by typing; three sections with exactly two hairlines at `--sp-6`; results state 8 REMOVED into a dirty helper and **state 14 ADDED**; states 1-7/9/11-13 unchanged in trigger and wording (R-F4). Appendix F revised **with superseded passages MARKED and left legible** (175 → 404 lines) — a reversal without the original reasoning reads as drift. Frozen needles moved in LOCKSTEP with **NEGATIVE pins** so the removed buttons cannot silently return (⚠ **C5: the pins live in `server_pane.rs`, NOT `design_round3.rs` as the intent's G3 stated** — `design_round3.rs` has zero server-pane coupling, while `server_pane.rs` pinned the four removed buttons and would have failed the instant the redesign landed). Mockups committed SANITIZED (F3R). **Scope held: UI + tests + docs only — no `src-tauri/src` change, no new backend command, no qsc API change, ZERO dependency motion, no colour or token change; `design_round2.rs`/`design_system.rs`/`design_round3.rs` byte-identical by `cmp`.** **PHASE 2b (qsl-desktop #11, D-0011, merge `b4ea47e7`, `[rust]` green, 73/0/1):** the three defects the live flight found (see D-1305 §7), each with a regression pin **verified as a POSITIVE CONTROL** — against the merged defective main exactly the three fail and the other ten pass. **THE CENSUS CORRECTED SIX THINGS IN THE INTENT'S OWN TEXT** (C1 ENG-0072's false premise; C2 "validate everything first" is not fully possible; C3 the mockups draw a CA path the app cannot know, since `relay_ca_file_show` returns `{configured, path_hash}` only; C4 R-D3's wording beats the mockups'; C5 the wrong pin file; C6 R-E6's "may" → "does"). **THREE OPERATOR-RULED FLAGS**, each folded into the rule it modifies: **F1R** *remove it* also clears the results block, broadening state 10's trigger to "any change to what the app will use" and making the reference mockups PART CATALOGUES rather than reachable states; **F2R** hairline padding `--sp-6` (32px) — the mockup's 30px sat exactly between `--sp-x28` and `--sp-6` with no nearer step, and no new token was added; **F3R** the mockups commit SANITIZED, since `qsl-desktop` is PUBLIC and the captured markup used a private host as its illustrative example (the originals are deliberately NOT restated in the committed files or the decision log — a redaction record written naively re-leaks what it redacts). **⚠ R-B1 AMENDED (Director ruling 2026-07-25):** C2 asserted the URL, unlike the CA path, could be validated WITHOUT writing. That was FALSE and was found false at implementation — the app registers nine relay commands and **none is validate-only**; `relay_config_set` runs `normalize_relay_endpoint` AND writes in the same call. That put R-B1 (vault writes first, settings.json last) and R-B2 (a malformed address persists NOTHING, on Save AND Test) in direct conflict. **RULED: R-B2's guarantee GOVERNS; R-B1's vault-first ordering is AMENDED to address-first** — *an absolute stated guarantee outranks unexplained write ordering; partial-commit-on-vault-failure is acceptable because state 14 reports it honestly and a re-test heals it.* The accepted cost is stated rather than hidden: if a vault write fails the address has already been saved. **D610's C2 text was NOT rewritten** — the directive is sha-pinned in the queue block, so amending it in place would break that pin and quietly rewrite an approved document; it is superseded in qsl-desktop D-0010 and here (Director-ruled: the supersession pointer is the correct discipline, no re-pin). No public/production/crypto-complete/bug-free claim. Result class **SERVER_PANE_REDESIGN_PANE_PASS**; the overall class is asserted at D-1305 on the flown acceptance.

- **ID:** D-1305
  - **Title:** NA-0674 closeout — Server pane redesign: the live acceptance flight was FLOWN and PASSED, and ⚠ it found THREE defects the 70-test suite did not; ENG-0072 CLOSED with its premise marked, ENG-0074 FILED; the queue returns to `READY=NONE | HIGHEST_NA=0674 | HIGHEST_D=1305`
  - **Date:** 2026-07-25

  - **Goal IDs:** G1
  - **Decision:** Close NA-0674. The implementation (D-1304) is on qsl-desktop main across #10 (`a836eaf`) and #11 (`b4ea47e7`); this closeout ships governance + acceptance only (docs_only), so the full suites correctly do not re-run here — **#10/#11's CI plus the operator's flight are the evidence, not this docs_only green.** ✅ **THE LIVE ACCEPTANCE FLIGHT WAS FLOWN AND PASSED** (operator-flown 2026-07-25 against the LAN relay rig over real TLS, no mocks; 25 screenshots in `/srv/qbuild/evidence/NA-0674/flight/`, per-state record in `flight_results.md`, per-check narrative in `docs/governance/evidence/NA-0674_as_built.md §6`). **ALL SEVEN PROBE OUTCOMES** exercised, plus states 9, 10, 11, 12 and 14. ⚠ **State 13 ("Couldn't start the connection test") is recorded NOT EXERCISED** — the generic client-build fallback, for which no reachable trigger was found; it is not counted as flown. **State 14 required DELIBERATE FAULT INJECTION**, because with the commit path's guards **no user input can fail a commit step**; the injection, a first attempt that FAILED, and the revert are recorded in full (`fault_injection_state14.txt`). ⚠ **That failed first attempt is itself a positive finding: qsc HARDENS its own config directory to 0700 immediately before every vault write (`vault/mod.rs:852`), so `chmod 0555` was self-healed and the save succeeded** — a vault directory loosened by any means is re-tightened at the next secret write. The fault that worked was a *directory* at the temp path, which `fs::remove_file` cannot clear. **THREE HEADLINE CONFIRMATIONS:** R-A2 — a wrong token typed then tested returned "Token rejected", where the pre-lane build would have probed the STORED token and said "Connected" (the trap this lane exists to remove, gone); R-E1 — **8 placeholder dots for a 64-character token**, length not leaked; C6 — "Settings saved." present on the committed Test and ABSENT on the clean one, so the append is real feedback rather than decoration. **⚠ THE LANE'S MOST TRANSFERABLE RESULT — THE FLIGHT FOUND THREE DEFECTS THE 70-TEST SUITE DID NOT**, all in D-0010's own code, all fixed in D-0011: **(a)** the dirty helper claimed "not saved" about settings that WERE saved (`renderDirty()` ran before the R-B5 echo, so the field still held raw text while `savedRelayUrl` held the normalized form — invisible unless the two differ, which WHATWG IPv4 shorthand `https://192` → `https://0.0.0.192` exposed); **(b)** a stale "Testing…" persisted under the inline address error, the pane asserting a test was running when none had been attempted — the failed-commit path awaited `refreshServerState()` BEFORE clearing the panel, and that call reaches `relay_token_show`/`relay_ca_file_show`, **both on the process-wide SERIAL blocking gate**, so a probe still in flight against a dead address parked the await for the whole TCP timeout; **(c)** state 14 opened with a raw `vault_write_failed`, `mapErr` having fallen through to `String(e)` and been concatenated onto the front of a sentence. **(b) was a REASONING ERROR, not a typo, and it generalises:** C2(b) requires re-reading live state after a **PARTIAL** commit because something landed; R-B2 guarantees a validation failure persists **NOTHING**, so that branch has nothing to re-read — applying the obligation to a branch it does not cover is what put a gated call in front of the panel clear. **No design ruling changed** — Appendix F already specified the correct behaviour in all three cases. Both user-visible defects were RE-FLOWN and confirmed fixed, and the (b) re-flight finally flew the malformed-address check properly (the earlier attempt had used a valid address), proving R-B2 three ways at once: inline error, no results card, and `settings.json` unchanged **on disk**. **VERIFICATION METHOD: all 25 screenshots were read by the executor and compared to the EXACT shipped copy** — nothing rests on eyeballing or on live verbal confirmation alone; that pass CORRECTED one entry (state 12's evidence is `10-59-47`, not `10-56-13`). **FILINGS AND RECORDS: ENG-0072 CLOSED** by the PHASE-1 fix, **with its stated premise MARKED as superseded by measurement, not silently rewritten** — the filing's reasoning is part of the record and the correction is only legible next to what it corrects. **ENG-0074 FILED** — the ENG-0072 fix is now load-bearing and nothing observes it; *the pre-fix world was dangerous but VISIBLE, every executor knew to check; the post-fix world is safe but INVISIBLE, and a silent regression there is strictly worse than the original defect because the discipline that used to catch it has been correctly retired*; the remedy (the EFFECTIVE `user.email` in `qwork`'s existing startup proof) is Director-deferred to review Lane C or the next spine tooling touch. **ENG-0073 discharged by construction.** **ENG-0064 REPRODUCED** on this lane's two-repo seat and noted on its entry; Director-ruled a candidate for the same tooling touch as ENG-0074. **THREE DIRECTOR NOTES RECORDED: (i) OBS-I** — desktop CI runs clippy WITHOUT `--all-targets`, hiding 5 pre-existing errors on main; folded into **review Lane C's** scope alongside the safety scan and cargo-audit, **and the 5 errors are to be fixed there**; the same class as the spine-leak gap — a check whose scope is narrower than the thing it is believed to protect. **(ii) OBS-J** — as above. **(iii) OBS-M** — state 13's unreachability is carried as a look-at note into the **lane-3 (messaging) intent**: correct defensive code today, but if a future lane cannot construct a trigger either it may be dead code rather than a state, and messaging will build the client on more paths. **RIG REACHABILITY CORRECTION ACCEPTED (Director):** the build host **CAN** reach the rig's LAN address — the standing "AP isolation" warning is stale and the handoff notes are corrected at next refresh. DOC-PROG-004 Step 5 progressed (the Server pane's interaction model is now flight-proven, and the reversal is recorded with its reasoning). No public/production/crypto-complete/bug-free claim. Result class **SERVER_PANE_REDESIGN_PASS**. Queue → `READY=NONE | HIGHEST_NA=0674 | HIGHEST_D=1305` (takes effect on merge). ENG-0051 (messaging) is the next product lane; the Logs pane (ENG-0058), the rail toggle (round-4b), contacts and onboarding remain later work.

Deltas are recorded **by FIELD NAME ONLY, never `original → replacement`** (`docs/governance/evidence/NA-0676_as_built.md`, `/srv/qbuild/evidence/NA-0676/tier1_delta.md`). **⚠ FLAG-B3 IS DROPPED — ITS PREMISE WAS MEASURED FALSE.** B3 ruled the three satellite hits be fixed in-lane because *"Lane C cannot adopt a gate in a repo that fails it on day one."* Measured against the D613 §2a tiering the operator ruled at C2: the two `/srv/qbuild` and `/home/victor` hits are **Tier 2a — not scanned at all**, and the retired-rig host name is **Tier 2b — added-line scoped**, so a pre-existing tracked line cannot fail it. **The Tier-1 instrument returns exit 0 on both satellites unfixed**; they already pass the gate Lane C will install. **The source of the error is D612 §2 as drafted:** it defines Tier 1 as "network-identifying + personal identity" and then lists those three Tier-2-class hits underneath it — an internal inconsistency in the directive that the B3 ruling then adopted. Found by a case-insensitive read, not by the tool. **A word-boundary-anchored gate misses the literal whenever it is embedded in an identifier, a snake_case symbol or a compound token**, which is precisely the shape Lane C is about to install as a merge gate. **⚠ THE SUBSTITUTION CONVENTION IS A RULING, NOT A DEVIATION:** D612 §4.2 offered RFC 5737 TEST-NET for command/config-shaped text, but every such case in this tree proved to be a **quotation of observed output** — a Caddyfile as deployed, a certificate SAN as issued, a `ca-set`/`server-info` transcript as it ran, a GUI footer as it rendered — not a template anyone would copy. **Substituting a plausible literal inside a quotation would fabricate an observation that was never made.** Surfaced before acting; the operator ruled **`<lan-address>` uniformly, no TEST-NET anywhere — "quotations must never contain fabricated observations."** **MEANING WAS CHECKED BY READING, AND THE CHECK CAUGHT REAL DAMAGE:** the backstop substitution introduced four grammatical breaks, all fixed before commit; an exhaustive artifact re-scan then returned five further matches, **all five verified PRE-EXISTING in `HEAD`** (enumeration letters such as "PR-A the crate split") and correctly left alone. **TIER 2 WAS NOT TOUCHED**, per B1: `/srv/qbuild` (4,184 hits) and `/home/victor` (1,153) are documented operational facts that `DOC-OPS-006` §3/§5a depends on to say where directives, proof files and tooling live, and the two remote account names and the retired rig's host name were ruled out of Tier 1; the full Tier-2 census is published in the as-built as **deliberate, recorded residue** carrying that rationale. **GIT HISTORY RETAINS EVERY ORIGINAL AND WAS NOT REWRITTEN** — a rewrite would force-push every published repository, break every recorded sha in `DECISIONS.md`/`TRACEABILITY.md`/the journal, invalidate the `qsc` rev pins in `qsl-desktop`, and violate GH007's no-force-push rule. The policy goal is a **clean current tree and clean future commits**; the disclosure already made is not undone by this lane, and the lane does not claim otherwise. Result class **`INFRA_SANITIZE_TIER1_PASS`**. Queue → `READY=NONE | HIGHEST_NA=0677 | HIGHEST_D=1307`; **NA-0677 (Lane C, D613 APPROVED) is next and MUST follow this lane** (D613 §3), and the operator promotes it.

- **ID:** D-1308
  - **Title:** NA-0677 impl-evidence — the operator-infrastructure literal gate lands in all four repositories, including the spine that leaked; the intent's "port the existing job" premise was false and the job name would have collided with a required context
  - **Date:** 2026-07-25
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G4
  - **Decision:** Land the infra-literal gate in this repository, completing the four-repo set per **QSL-DIR-2026-07-25-613 (D613, APPROVED 2026-07-25, amended twice; sha256 `586ae25a797342bd066b2ebd152213b00df6014b9e8a7fba19d57fe0a9b95a51`, 446 lines)**. Implementation across the satellites is merged: **qsl-desktop #13 (D-0014, `44237b23`)**, **qsl-server #65 (D-0015)**, **qsl-attachments #41 (D-0012)**; the `/srv/qbuild/tools` half is local commits `410221d` (ENG-0074 + ENG-0064) and `9273417` (the operator-held plaintext name list), for which **there is no PR because that repository has no remote**. **⚠ THE INTENT'S PREMISE WAS FALSE, AND THIS REPOSITORY IS THE PROOF:** `scripts/ci/public_safety_gate.py:32-40` scans for private keys and cloud tokens and has never contained an address, path or host pattern (`git grep private_ipv4` = 0) — and **this is the repository whose tracked files carried a private LAN address across nine files, on pull requests that the required `public-safety` context passed green every time.** The failure was the pattern set, not the scan's scope. **⚠ THE NEW JOB IS DELIBERATELY NOT NAMED `public-safety` OR `advisories`.** Both names are already **required status contexts here**, produced by `public-ci.yml`; reusing either would put two check runs with one name in front of branch protection on the single repository where fourteen contexts are actually enforced. The gate is therefore **entirely additive** — new workflow file `.github/workflows/infra-literal-scan.yml`, new job id `infra-literal-scan`, and **`public-ci.yml` byte-untouched** (verified: zero diff). Collision against the live required-contexts list was checked by API, not assumed: **NONE**. **THE SCANNER IS BYTE-IDENTICAL ACROSS ALL FOUR REPOSITORIES** (`cmp`-proven at each landing); the pattern set is deliberately **not forked** — one source of truth for one question. **TIERS:** Tier 1 (network-identifying literals and personal identity) over the **whole tracked tree**, failing on any hit; Tier 2b (low-frequency private names) over **added lines only**; **Tier 2a (the build-root and home paths) NOT SCANNED AT ALL** — the governance convention cites every directive and lane intent by absolute path, so those literals appear in roughly 60% of this repository's commits (measured at D613 C8: 17/30 and 10/30) and a gate on them would be switched off within a week. They remain published as **recorded residue** from NA-0676. **This tree scans CLEAN at landing: 2,280 files, 599,746 lines examined, zero hits, in ~12 seconds** — green on arrival only because NA-0676 cleaned it first, which is the sequencing D613 §3 required. **THE PRIVATE NAMES ARE SALTED SHA-256 DIGESTS, NOT TEXT:** these repositories are public, and a pattern file naming them would republish exactly what NA-0676 removed **and** make the Tier-1 whole-tree scan hit its own pattern file — verified against a scratch repository, not assumed. **Operator ruling on that trade (2026-07-25, recorded at D613 §2a-ter):** approved, with the plaintext list held operator-side so the digests can be regenerated and audited, and with §2a's one-screen reviewability explicitly preserved for the tier structure, class labels and structural regexes while being **deliberately given up for the name values**. ⚠ One part of that ruling is **not achievable and is recorded rather than fudged**: the **salt must remain in the public file**, because the scanner hashes candidate tokens at scan time and cannot compare them against stored digests without it — an operator-held salt means the gate cannot run in public CI at all. The public file states plainly that the salt only defeats a **precomputed** lookup and is not a secret from anyone who already knows a name; **the protection that matters is the names' absence from the tree**. **ANCHORING (operator ruling L1):** no naked `\b`-anchoring — a word boundary does not match inside `HOST_<name>`, which is the case NA-0676 was blind to. Matching is **token-wise**, splitting on non-alphanumerics **and** camelCase transitions, after raw substring matching was **rejected by its own positive control** for firing on every identifier that merely spans a camelCase seam. **EVERY CONTROL RAN RED FIRST, IN EVERY REPOSITORY** — a gate is a property of the repo it runs in, not of the script, so the proof was re-run rather than inherited. In this repository both the embedded-literal control and, more to the point, **the private-address control** fail the scan and pass once removed: *the exact class that leaked here, seeded again, now caught.* Additionally the gate **caught its own implementation** on the desktop PR (the scanner's docstring had used a real host name as an example), and a **vacuous-pass defect was found by reading the CI log rather than the check mark** — the scan printed `clean` identically whether it examined 438 lines or zero, and now reports `clean (tree; N files, M lines examined)` and **refuses to report a pass over an empty input** in tree and diff modes (but not in staged mode, where a deletion-only commit legitimately has no added lines). **⚠ THE NEW JOB IS ADVISORY, NOT BLOCKING, IN ALL FOUR REPOSITORIES.** The three satellites require exactly one context (`rust`); this repository's required list does not include `infra-literal-scan`. The jobs run and report but **cannot block a merge** until the operator adds them — a branch-protection change, which is the operator's act and which no part of this lane performs. **Green is not the same as blocking, and nothing here claims otherwise.** Result class **`CI_HARDENING_PASS`** at the closeout (D-1309).

- **ID:** D-1309
  - **Title:** NA-0677 closeout — the operator-infrastructure literal gate is live in all four repositories, ENG-0074 and ENG-0064 CLOSED with their proof gaps closed too; ⚠ the new checks are ADVISORY until branch protection is updated, and that is the one thing this lane deliberately did not do
  - **Date:** 2026-07-25
  - **Status:** Accepted
  - **Goal IDs:** G4
  - **Decision:** Close NA-0677, and with it the three-lane review series opened by the 2026-07-25 all-repo review. Implementation is merged across all four repositories — **qsl-desktop #13 `44237b23` (D-0014)**, **qsl-server #65 `6ad078c2` (D-0015)**, **qsl-attachments #41 `999f3293` (D-0012)**, **qsl-protocol #1655 `27134984` (D-1308)** — plus two local `/srv/qbuild/tools` commits, **`410221d`** (ENG-0074 + ENG-0064) and **`9273417`** (the operator-held plaintext name list), **for which there is no PR because that repository has no remote**. Executed per **QSL-DIR-2026-07-25-613 (D613, APPROVED 2026-07-25, amended twice; sha256 `586ae25a797342bd066b2ebd152213b00df6014b9e8a7fba19d57fe0a9b95a51`, 446 lines)**. **⚠ THE INTENT'S PREMISE WAS FALSE:** there was nothing to port. The spine's required `public-safety` job scans for private keys and cloud tokens and has never contained an address, path or host pattern — **which is exactly why it ran green on every pull request that published a private LAN address across nine of this repository's tracked files.** The failure was the pattern set, not the scan's scope, and the lane built the missing set rather than moving one. **RESULT CLASS `CI_HARDENING_PASS`.**
  - **What the green does and does not prove.** The #1655 implementation PR classified `runtime_and_workflow`, so the **full suites ran** — 36 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail, the two skips being `macos-qsc-full-serial` and `qsc-linux-full-suite`, which key off `qsc/src` changes that PR did not make. **That green carries information.** ⚠ **This closeout is `docs_only`, so the behavioural suites correctly SKIP on its merge and its green proves the governance edit is well-formed and NOTHING ELSE.** The evidence for the gate is the controls, not any check mark.
  - **⚠ EVERY CONTROL RAN RED FIRST, IN EVERY REPOSITORY, AND THREE OF THEM REJECTED WHAT THEY WERE TESTING.** A gate is a property of the repository it runs in, not of the script, so the proof was re-run rather than inherited. **(a) The embedded-literal control rejected the matcher design:** raw substring matching caught `SOME_<name>_THING` but also fired on every identifier that merely *spans* a camelCase seam — a 7-character host name sits inside `setServerBusy` and `commitServerSettings`, burying the real hit under eleven false positives from qsl-desktop's own UI code. Matching became **token-wise**, splitting on non-alphanumerics **and** camelCase transitions, which keeps every embedded case and drops the spanning ones. **This is not a word boundary under another name** — `\b` fails on `HOST_<name>`, the case the gate exists for. **(b) The Tier-1 control rejected itself as invalid:** the seed file was never staged, and `--mode tree` scans `git ls-files`, so the run came back GREEN where RED was expected — correct gate behaviour, invalid test, caught only because the expected result was written down before the run. **(c) The gate caught its own implementation:** run against qsl-desktop #13, Tier 1 failed on the scanner's own docstring, which had used a real host name to illustrate the embedded case — **the fifth occurrence in four days of a record naming what it redacts, and the first caught by a machine rather than a person re-reading.** In the spine, the control that matters is the **private-address** one: the exact class that leaked from this repository, seeded again, now caught.
  - **⚠ AND THE GATE HAD A WAY TO PASS WITHOUT LOOKING, FOUND BY READING THE CI LOG RATHER THAN THE CHECK MARK.** The first run printed `infra-literal-scan: clean (diff)` — a line printed identically whether the scan examined 438 added lines or **zero**. A green that cannot be distinguished from a no-op **is the exact defect this gate was built to answer**, reproduced inside the fix for it. The scan now reports what it examined (`clean (tree; 2283 files, 600140 lines examined)`) and **refuses to report a pass over an empty input** (exit 2) in `tree` and `diff` modes — where empty means a broken checkout or an unfetched base ref — but **deliberately NOT in `staged` mode**, where a deletion-only or rename-only commit legitimately has no added lines and refusing would block honest commits from the pre-commit hook.
  - **The design, and the operator rulings it rests on.** **Tiers:** Tier 1 (network-identifying literals and personal identity) whole-tree, failing on any hit; Tier 2b (low-frequency private names) added-lines only; **Tier 2a (build-root and home paths) not scanned at all**, because the citation convention puts them in ~60% of spine commits (17/30 and 10/30, measured at D613 C8) and a gate on them would be switched off within a week — they remain NA-0676's published residue. **Digests (operator-approved, D613 §2a-ter):** the private names ship as salted SHA-256 digests because these repositories are public and a pattern file naming them would republish exactly what NA-0676 removed **and** make the Tier-1 scan hit its own pattern file — verified against a scratch repository, not assumed. The plaintext list is **operator-held** so the digests can be regenerated and audited; §2a's one-screen reviewability is preserved for the tier structure, class labels and structural regexes and **deliberately traded away for the name values**. ⚠ **One part of that ruling is not achievable and is recorded rather than fudged: the salt must remain in the public file**, because the scanner hashes candidate tokens at scan time and cannot compare them against stored digests without it; an operator-held salt means the gate cannot run in public CI at all, and an env-var or CI-secret salt breaks fork PRs and local runs. The public file states plainly that the salt defeats only a **precomputed** lookup and is not a secret from anyone who already knows a name — **the protection that matters is the names' absence from the tree**. **Anchoring (ruling L1):** no naked `\b`-anchoring; noise tuned by the tier structure, never by narrowing a pattern. **Pre-commit call site (ruling L2):** `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` runs the **same** instrument over the staged set, opt-in via `core.hooksPath`; the pattern set is **not forked**; it proved trivial, so the STOP fence was not needed. CI is the enforcement — hooks are not cloned. **OBS-AN (ruling L3): no action taken here.**
  - **⚠ A COLLISION CAUGHT BY CHECKING RATHER THAN ASSUMING.** The spine already publishes **required** contexts named `public-safety` **and** `advisories`. Naming the new job either of those would have put two check runs with one name in front of branch protection **on the single repository where fourteen contexts are enforced**. The live required-contexts list was read by API before choosing; the spine's job is therefore `infra-literal-scan`, in its own new workflow file, with **`public-ci.yml` byte-untouched (zero diff, verified)**. D613 §7 had anticipated the adjacent risk — do not edit the 2,599-line gate — but not the name clash.
  - **ENG-0074 CLOSED**, implemented as a **fail-closed assertion** rather than the recorded line its filing recommended, because the operator's Lane-C instruction said *assert*: `qwork_assert_seat_identity()` on **both** seat paths plus `new_checkout.sh`, reading the **effective** identity so an inherited-from-global value is visible rather than masked. `seat_user_name` / `seat_user_email` are also written to the KV and both JSON proof writers. **The filing's own framing now holds in both directions: the pre-fix world was dangerous but visible, the post-fix world was safe but invisible, and it is now safe AND observed.**
  - **ENG-0064 CLOSED** in the same tools commit per FLAG-C4. The root cause was one line: the old guard could not tell an operator-set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` from the one qbuild exported moments earlier in the same invocation. **The operator-set case is preserved** — that was the whole risk in the change and it got its own control. ⚠ **The baseline, captured before the fix, is worse than every previous report: on this lane's four-repo seat, three of four repos were wrong** — the defect scales with the seat. Its proof gap is closed too, by a fail-closed assertion and a `cargo_target_is_own_registered` proof field, so a recurrence is greppable across lanes instead of depending on an executor noticing. **Sighted four times before it was fixed.**
  - **`enforce_admins` — DONE and VERIFIED, not pending.** The census observed `qsl-attachments` at `enforce_admins: false` while the other three read `true`, and **reported it without acting** (branch protection is the operator's act and outside D613's scope). The operator flipped it on 2026-07-25 and the executor **verified the result independently by API: `enforce_admins.enabled = true`, with the required-contexts list still `["rust"]`, confirming the change touched only what it was meant to.** All four repositories now read `true`; the asymmetry is closed.
  - **⚠ THE ONE THING STILL OWED, AND IT IS THE OPERATOR'S: the four new checks are ADVISORY, not blocking.** `public-safety` in `qsl-desktop`, `qsl-server` and `qsl-attachments` (each of which requires exactly one context, `rust`) and `infra-literal-scan` in `qsl-protocol` (whose fourteen required contexts do not include it) **run and report on every pull request but cannot block a merge until they are added to the required sets.** **Green is not the same as blocking, and nothing in this lane claims otherwise.** No part of this lane made a branch-protection API call for the required sets; promoting them is a deliberate operator act, and until it happens the gate is a very good early-warning system and not a gate.
  - **DOC-OPS-006 §3 updated:** the operator-side publication scanner is **no longer the source of truth** for these patterns — the committed script is, and when the two disagree the committed script wins.
  - **Not claimed:** that the gate has ever caught a real leak. It has not, **by construction** — NA-0676 cleaned every tree first, which is why every Tier-1 scan is green on arrival (D613 §3's sequencing). The gate's value is **prospective**, and the controls are what make that a reasonable bet rather than a hope. No security, production, crypto-complete or vulnerability-free claim is made or implied.

  - **The green carries information here.** #66 changed `src/`, so `rust` compiled and ran the code: `rust` PASS · `public-safety` PASS · `advisories` PASS on the exact reviewed commit. Slice 1 therefore built ONE subsystem and spent its care on not breaking the other.
