## D-1413 — P-FACADE / ONE FACADE, TWO FRONT-ENDS: NO CLI MODE THE GUI CANNOT SEE — THE OPERATOR'S RULING MADE DURABLE IN THE PROJECT

- **Date/Lane:** 2026-08-29 · recorded by NA-0771 (`D-1412`) as a **rider on the promotion PR**, records only · Goals G4
- **Source order:** `ORDER_one_facade_two_frontends_20260828.md`, sha256 `b812117e844862f26aeebd99f5df66d0e37533364297d96925be7c56d322b594`, banked 444 at `/srv/qbuild/operator/method/` per `SR-14`, all 64 digits compared mechanically with a negative control on the comparator.
- **Standing:** a recorded **PROPERTY, not a numbered rule** — RESTRAINT (`D-2`/`R305`); `SR-26` spent the numbered-rule slot for that act.

**THE OPERATOR'S RULING, VERBATIM (2026-08-28):** *"I agree, make it durable in the project."*

**AND THE TEXT THE OPERATOR BLESSED, REPRODUCED VERBATIM** (the Director's recommendation, uploaded by the operator as the blessed text):

> *"What I'd recommend, and will fold into the sequencing order at the next revision: no new user-facing CLI affordance without a matching GUI affordance. New protocol behavior enters through the library facade the GUI calls; the CLI gets a thin verb over the same facade and nothing more. One facade, two front-ends, no mode the GUI can't see. That keeps the test harness and the diagnostics, and stops the drift."*

**THE PROPERTY.**

> **P-FACADE** — Product behaviour enters through the library facade the GUI calls. Every CLI subcommand, flag or persisted config key is ONE of:
> **(i)** a **THIN VERB** over that facade — the same call the GUI makes, with no mode, setting or persisted state the GUI cannot see; or
> **(ii)** declared **LAB-ONLY** at its definition site, with the reason. A lab-only affordance may OBSERVE (status, markers, diagnostics) or ADDRESS for diagnosis (e.g. `--mailbox`); it **never SELECTS A PROTOCOL MODE** and **never PERSISTS a setting** that changes the product's behaviour for a user.
> A fixture or workflow script that uses a lab-only affordance names it as such.

**THE TWO PAID-FOR INSTANCES, WHICH ARE WHY THIS IS A PROPERTY AND NOT AN OPINION.** `--ack-mode` was **(ii) without the declaration and WITH a mode** — the exact thing the property forbids — and cost two days to retire (`NA-0770`, `D-1411`). `--mailbox` is **(ii) and stays, declared** — a lab knob a fixture misused, and **187 days of red** (`ENG-0192`/`NA-0737`).

**WHAT THE CLI KEEPS, STATED SO THE PROPERTY IS NOT READ AS A RETIREMENT.** The CLI stays: it is the test harness and the only diagnostic window into protocol state until the GUI's diagnostics lane ships. What goes is the CLI's ability to grow a behaviour the product does not have.

**THE PREMISES, RE-MEASURED BY THIS SEAT RATHER THAN ADOPTED — AND ONE DID NOT REPRODUCE.**
- **(a) CONFIRMED EXACTLY.** `qsl-desktop` `src-tauri/Cargo.toml:23` is `qsc = { git = "https://github.com/QuantumShieldLabs/qsl-protocol", rev = "b3ae24b430e516d9b43bb654905c7992beb59ce7" }` — a **git LIBRARY dependency**. `Command::new` / `std::process` across `src-tauri/src/*.rs`: **ZERO**, the grep exiting 1, with a positive control on the same needle proving it can match. ⇒ **the GUI never runs the `qsc` binary.**
- **(b) CONFIRMED AND WIDER THAN THE ORDER STATES.** The order names five modules (`facade`, `vault`, `transport`, `identity`, `store`) as *"top paths"*. Measured at desktop main `11f695df`, the GUI calls **eight**: `qsc::facade` (36), `qsc::transport` (15), `qsc::vault` (12), `qsc::identity` (10), `qsc::output` (5), `qsc::store` (4), `qsc::adversarial` (2), `qsc::vault_unlocked` (1). The order's five are the top five by count; the full set is recorded here so a later reader does not treat five as the boundary.
- **(c) NOT REPRODUCED, AND THE INSTRUMENT IS THE SUSPECT.** The order states *"111 of 144 files invoke the binary via `assert_cmd::cargo::cargo_bin!("qsc")` (`tests/common/mod.rs:133/140/160`)"*. The **144** reproduces exactly at the order's own base `3b685e79`. The **111** did not reproduce under four needles, which **bracket** it: direct `cargo_bin!` ∪ the three cited helpers = **109**; direct ∪ the two spawning constructors = **107**; direct ∪ `mod common` = **113**; direct ∪ any `common::` = **113**. ⚠ **The order's figure is NOT contradicted**: a census instrument that cannot reproduce a known answer is the suspect, not the answer (`NA-0758`'s recorded lesson). The residue between 109 and 113 is four files that declare `mod common` without reaching the binary through it. **The property does not turn on the exact count** — it turns on the shape, which is confirmed: the overwhelming majority of protocol tests reach the binary and the GUI reaches it **zero** times. At this lane's base `39cd39e6` the denominator is **145** (Lane A added one test file).

**THE CONSUMER, SO THE PROPERTY DOES NOT DECAY.** The kickoff template — `SR-26`'s consumer — gains the checklist line at sec 3(a), landed in this same PR at `docs/ops/KICKOFF_TEMPLATE.md`. A **MECHANICAL** consumer is **NAMED, NOT BUILT**: a source-shape test over `cmd/mod.rs` and the persisted-config writer asserting every persisted key carries a facade or lab-only tag — a candidate for the CI-migration lane.

**IMMEDIATE APPLICATION.** Binds every lane from the `ENG-0252` repair forward. First test: **this lane** — the kickoff's sec 6 forbids adding a CLI flag or config key, citing P-FACADE by name. Second: the inviter repair, where any `handshake poll` facade verb the GUI's tick calls is **(i)** and the CLI's existing `handshake poll` becomes a thin verb over the same call, not a second implementation.

## D-1414 — L1–L5 / FIVE LEVERS FOR THE GUI BUILD, BLESSED — AND AMENDMENT 1 TO P-FACADE

- **Date/Lane:** 2026-08-29 · recorded by NA-0771 (`D-1412`) as a **rider on the promotion PR**, records only · Goals G4
- **Source order:** `ORDER_gui_build_levers_20260828.md`, sha256 `e42d0e69ac5c7443b6edf6a091b3b5bc85ca5d04bb48362cb37a0513841d2944`, banked 444 at `/srv/qbuild/operator/method/` per `SR-14`, all 64 digits compared mechanically with a negative control on the comparator.
- **Amends by reference:** `ORDER_one_facade_two_frontends_20260828.md` (`b812117e…b594`, recorded here as `D-1413`). **L2 is its first amendment, mark-don't-rewrite; that file is not edited and `D-1413` is not rewritten.**
- **Standing:** recorded **PROPERTIES, not numbered rules** — RESTRAINT.

**THE OPERATOR'S RULING, VERBATIM (2026-08-28):** *"lets make those happen."*

**THE FIVE, IN THE WORDS THE OPERATOR BLESSED:**

> **1.** *Test the facade directly.* The GUI calls the library facade (15 functions), but the protocol is proven through the CLI binary (111 of 144 test files spawn it). So the thing the GUI actually calls has the **LEAST** direct coverage. Add in-process facade tests — no subprocess, seconds not minutes — proving the same property each CLI test proves. Start with the inviter repair's facade verb.
> **2.** *Keep the Tauri command layer as thin as the CLI.* 27 commands on Aug 16, **43 now**. Same rule as the one-facade order: commands wrap the facade, no logic of their own.
> **3.** *Move the pin with the facade.* Every protocol lane that adds a facade function for the GUI bumps the desktop pin in the same arc (the cross-repo shape already in the rules).
> **4.** *Run the two pure-UI fixes now.* Contacts scroll and the busy-indicator suppression do not depend on the inviter repair. The other four deferred fixes wait as planned.
> **5.** *Every GUI lane ships one driver test for the screen it builds.* Live flights stay the acceptance standard.
> *Not changed: zero-npm, vanilla HTML/CSS/JS.*

**THE RULINGS, EACH WITH ITS CONSUMER.**

**L1 — FACADE TESTS.** Any lane that adds or changes a facade function ships an **in-process** test of that function proving the property the corresponding CLI test proves, **with a red arm**. CONSUMER: the kickoff-template line from `D-1413` **extends** to *"…and name its facade test"*. FIRST INSTANCE: the inviter repair's specification (`NA-0768`); **the `ENG-0252` lane carries one only if it touches the facade** — and its kickoff sec 1 makes the facade conditional, adding that if it is touched, **L1 applies and the lane becomes cross-repo by L3**. NOT ORDERED: a retroactive sweep of the 15 existing facade functions — named as a candidate lane once the suite-runtime work lands, **its value measured, not assumed**.

**L2 — THIN COMMAND LAYER (amendment 1 to P-FACADE).** The GUI's Tauri command layer is **front-end #2** and is held to the same property as the CLI: a command wraps one facade call and carries no protocol logic. **A command that needs logic is a facade function that does not exist yet — file it in protocol; do not build it in the desktop.** CONSUMER: the kickoff-template line applies to desktop lanes verbatim. FIRST INSTANCE: the UI-fix lane (L4) adds none and says so.

**L3 — THE PIN MOVES WITH THE FACADE.** A protocol lane that adds a facade function **for the GUI** is a cross-repo lane **BY CONSTRUCTION**: one planned stop at both open PRs, the desktop half carrying the pin bump to the protocol PR's merge commit, merge order by dependence (**protocol first**). **No separate pin lane later.** CONSUMER: the kickoff-template line. FIRST INSTANCE: the inviter repair.

**L4 — THE PURE-UI LANE, PROMOTED-CANDIDATE.** Two fixes, both measured by the Director at desktop main `11f695df` and both reproducing the packet's `05_ROADMAP` 2.4 / 2.5: **(a) CONTACTS LIST SCROLL** — `ui/style.css:499` `.list-pane` is a flex column with no `overflow-y`, so the window grows instead of the list scrolling; one CSS rule and a test that fails without it. **(b) BUSY INDICATOR ON EVERY TICK** — `#busy-indicator` (`ui/index.html:9`) is driven by the invoke wrapper's `pendingCalls` counter (`ui/main.js:15/18`) with no notion of source, while `relayScan({ source: "tick" })` at `:2004` and the `ev.source === "tick"` branch at `:3433` already exist. **OPERATOR-RULED IN THE PACKET AND UNCHANGED: suppress for tick-sourced calls ONLY; "suppress always" is REFUSED** — the indicator earns its keep on Connect. Coupled consequence, already ruled: once the tick is silent, the footer's declined-frame notice is the only evidence of background activity. ⚠ **FINDING CARRIED: NEITHER FIX IS FILED IN REPO TRUTH** — no declaring `ENG` heading in `docs/ops/IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER.md` at `3b685e79` (needles: *scroll*, *busy*, *tick-sourced*; positive control: `ENG-0248` declares), and the desktop repo carries no ledger. **The UI-fix lane FILES them as its first records act.** BOUNDS: zero protocol bytes, zero facade change, zero Tauri commands added, one driver test per fix. `SR-15` not triggered — no crypto, no lock, two UI files, no safety mechanism — **stated so it can be challenged**. CARRIED, NOT IN THAT LANE: a short delay before the indicator appears so fast local calls never flicker.

**L5 — ONE DRIVER TEST PER GUI LANE.** Every desktop lane that builds or changes a screen ships at least one behavioural test in `src-tauri/tests/gui_driver.rs` (the tauri-driver / WebDriver harness; six `#[ignore]` tests exist, `na0701_gui_a..f`), **red-armed**, run by the seat before the PR with its result in the stop. **Live operator flights remain the acceptance standard; the driver tests hold the line between flights.** CONSUMER: the kickoff-template line. FIRST INSTANCE: L4.

⚠ **THE `111 of 144` FIGURE INSIDE L1'S BLESSED TEXT IS QUOTED, NOT ADOPTED.** It is the operator-blessed wording and is reproduced verbatim as such. This seat could not reproduce it — see `D-1413`'s premise (c), where four needles bracket it at 107–113 and **the instrument, not the figure, is recorded as the suspect**. Nothing in L1 turns on the exact count.


## D-1409 — NA-0768 / THE INVITER REPAIR: COMPLETING RUNG 1 — THE PROMOTION, THE MENU ORDERED BEFORE ANY DESIGN, AND TWO DEAD DESIGNS CARRIED FORWARD AS INPUTS RATHER THAN RESUMED

### THE RULING

**PER-CONTACT ROUTE TOKENS: OUT FOR THE PRIMARY DEPLOYMENT** (one organization running the
relay for its members). Declined **with the measurement**. The Director's original *"per-contact
route tokens would close it"* was an overclaim, withdrawn before this lane began; the measured
form is **"the mechanism is not the remedy."**

**THE FOUR GROUNDS, each verified independently by the cold read as well as by this seat:**

- **G1 — C5 IS UNTOUCHED.** `invites.bundle` stores `canonical_bundle_bytes(kem_pk, sig_pk)`
  (`invite/mod.rs:235-249`), the account's long-term identity public keys, stable per account
  (`identity/mod.rs:566-580` returns the persisted self-identity). Every invite one account
  creates links to every other by byte equality. Route tokens do not touch it.
- **G2 — THE CLEARTEXT HANDSHAKE CORRELATOR.** The 16-byte `session_id` sits at a fixed offset
  in all three frame types (`handshake/mod.rs:22`, `:459`, `:541`, `:626`, `:685`); A1/A2 land
  in the responder's mailbox and B1 in the initiator's, so **the same correlator sits in frames
  stored in BOTH peers' mailboxes** and the relay pairs them by byte equality with no
  cryptography. Per-contact addresses do not close it. **This is the lane's best finding and it
  is filed separately as `F2`.**
- **G3 — THE GLOBAL ROUTE CAP.** `store.rs:382` and `:674` both `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM routes`;
  default 256, confirmed from the binary's own `--help` at 37ec8207. Per-contact tokens consume
  it N-fold.
- **G4 — THE PULL SIDE DOES NOT IMPROVE.** The session/IP join is structural and no relay-side
  cure exists at this base (NA-0768's menu `X1`: *"there is no multi-mailbox pull at this
  base"*). **Solid as reasoning; never run.**

**⚠ THE FIFTH GROUND IS STRUCK, EVERYWHERE IT APPEARED.** Earlier drafts rested part of the
verdict on an at-rest `routes.last_touched` timestamp-correlation signature. **The write does
not happen:** at 37ec8207 the post-pull `UPDATE` is guarded by `else if !seqs.is_empty()`
(`store.rs:783-787`), so an empty pull writes nothing and a pull on a never-pushed route
creates no row. It is **struck, not downgraded**, from all three places it was argued — the
stop's delta headline, this record's ground, and the document's T2 — and the verdict does not
need it.

**⚠ AND ONE CELL IS CORRECTED IN THE RULING'S DISFAVOUR, WITH A CREDIT IT NEVER TOOK.**
"Contact count becomes directly readable" moves from **(−) to 0**: T1 **already** leaks the
count by the same session/IP join on the send side — N distinct destinations in one session
*is* the contact count, today. And a **(+) no draft credited** appears: at T1 those
destinations are the recipients' **account-stable** addresses, so the relay can join them to
those recipients' own sessions and recover the graph *with identities*; per-contact addresses
break that join. ⇒ **the honest delta is smaller in both directions.** That is a better
argument for the ruling than the one it replaces, because it no longer rests on a cost that
measurement removed.

**⚠ THE RESERVATION IS A CONDITION, NOT A DESTINATION.** For the shared-relay and
sender's-relay deployments the send-side gain is real, but **the order's R1 is NOT
discharged for them either**: R1 forbids minting per-contact tokens until a ruling says what
they buy, against which relay, **and whether the pull side needs its own answer** — and no
pull-side answer is designed or scheduled. ⇒ **If the operator adopts a shared or public
relay, R1 remains in force. Re-open `D-1415` only after a pull-side answer exists to be
priced — separate sessions, routed pulls, or the relay-side multi-mailbox pull NA-0768's menu
calls `E5c` — and re-measure the send-side gain against that deployment's own table.** `E5c`
is the named prerequisite and it is out of NA-0768's bounds.

**THE SCOPE, IF IT IS EVER BUILT — named, not designed:** `vault/mod.rs` `:568`/`:573` and
`generate_default_route_token` `:726`/`:737` (one secret becomes a per-peer map);
`contacts/mod.rs::relay_self_inbox_route_token` `:60-69`; the three hand-out sites
`invite/mod.rs` `:1120→:1129` (**`invite_redeem_at`** — the order's *"invite create"* label is
corrected here), `:1354→:1372` (`invite_accept_at`), `:1416` (`invite_finish`); the poll over N
addresses; and **the relay's global route cap**, which no client-side design can satisfy alone.

### FOUR FINDINGS FILED (ledger entries; filed, not fixed)

**`F1` — qsl-server: DELETED MESSAGES PERSIST ON DISK. Severity P2.**
`store.rs:208-212` sets exactly `journal_mode=WAL`, `synchronous=FULL`, `foreign_keys=ON`;
needle count across `src/` for `secure_delete`, `wal_checkpoint`, `VACUUM`, `auto_vacuum`,
`journal_size_limit` is **zero**. Measured at 37ec8207 on a fully-drained mailbox: SQL reports
`routes` 0 rows and `messages` 0 rows while the raw files hold the message body ×3, its msg_id
×3, the `route_key` pseudonym ×9 and the `log_id` pseudonym ×2. `sqlite_sequence` additionally
retains a lifetime message count. **Privacy at rest; the org's disk encryption is the outer
control.** Remedy CANDIDATES named, none chosen: `PRAGMA secure_delete=ON`; periodic
`wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`; and the honest limit that filesystem-level residue remains. A
qsl-server lane; the relay-redeploy decision (ladder order R3.7) rides with it.

**`F2` — THE CLEARTEXT SESSION-ID CORRELATOR. A DESIGN finding.**
G2 above. The relay can pair handshake counterparts without any cryptography, and per-contact
tokens do not close it. The cure is a **protocol** change — a per-mailbox or encrypted
correlator — and belongs to the messaging epic's design pass and the ladder, **not to this
lane**. Filed so the obligation is inherited rather than rediscovered.

**`F3` — qsl-server DEFAULT LOGGING IS AN ACCIDENT, NOT A CONTRACT.**
The empty request log follows from `EnvFilter::from_default_env()`'s default level
(`main.rs:231-233`), not from a stated property, and can regress silently. A small hardening
item: **state the contract, test it** (a test asserting the log is empty after a scripted
exchange), and **consider what the nine `tracing::error!` sites should carry** — **one of
them (`lib.rs:1019`, inside `run_store`) sits on a live request path**; a second
(`lib.rs:480`) is the background retention sweeper, and the remaining seven are startup and
configuration.
⚠⚠ **AND REQUEST LOGGING IS ONE LINE AWAY, WHICH IS A STRONGER STATEMENT OF THIS FINDING'S
OWN THESIS:** at 37ec8207 `Cargo.toml` already declares
`tower-http = { version = "0.5", features = ["trace"] }` — the crate is linked and the
